# WELD: everything in one file

> WELD is a Laravel 13 app with Inertia and Vue that comes with the rest of the Wayne State stack already set up: sign-in, security headers, the standards check, code style and CI. Start your app from it.

The README and the Markdown twin of every page, joined. The index is https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/llms.txt. Written by Squire's agent-ready kit; do not edit.

---

## README

Source: https://nougat.snu.gs/enterprise-apps/weld/blob/HEAD/README.md

On Citadel it is served by the raw-PHP deploy layer in [`deploy/`](https://nougat.snu.gs/enterprise-apps/weld/blob/HEAD/deploy/): a Squire kit whose front controller serves `site/` behind HELMET's security headers. For local development, keep serving `site/` directly.

## WELD

**W**ired, **E**verything, **L**inked, **D**eployed. Many parts, one piece.

WELD is the whole Wayne State app stack joined into one application. Install it, deploy it, and every part is already
hooked up: sign-in, security headers, checks, coding standards, CI and the WayneUI interface. Think of it as the
Megazord, except it comes with a deploy script and nobody has to shout to make it combine.

### Documentation

The docs live at [site/docs/index.html](https://nougat.snu.gs/enterprise-apps/weld/blob/HEAD/site/docs/index.html) and ship to https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/. They are
built from `docs/` by the shared docs builder (`composer docs`) and checked in `composer ci`, so the page you read is
the page that ships: same source, same bead.

### Where the code lives

The canonical repository is on nougat: [enterprise-apps/weld](https://nougat.snu.gs/enterprise-apps/weld). git.wayne.edu and GitHub ([waynestate/weld](https://github.com/waynestate/weld)) are read-only mirrors of it.
Open issues and merge requests on nougat, not on the mirrors.
This moves to git.wayne.edu once it has CI runners. The weld is made on nougat; the mirrors only get the polished bead.

**Not to be confused with:** `weld:doctor` checks local setup only; standards checks are PROCTOR's.

### Get it

WELD is an app you start from, not a library you require. The Megazord ships in a repo, not a box.
Composer makes you a fresh copy, writes `.env`, generates the app key and runs the first migration:

```
composer create-project waynestate/weld my-app
cd my-app
npm ci
```

Or clone it, if you want the history too, and it is yours to rename:

```
git clone https://github.com/waynestate/weld.git my-app
cd my-app
composer install
php vendor/bin/advisor install --client=claude --write
npm ci
# Windows (PowerShell):
Copy-Item .env.example .env
# Linux/macOS:
cp .env.example .env
php artisan key:generate
```

The `advisor install` line writes `.mcp.json`, the MCP config that points Claude Code at ADVISOR's server; the file is git-ignored, because a committed `.mcp.json` would run a program on whoever opens the project. Set `ADVISOR_ENABLED=1` in `.env` to switch the advisor on. Running WELD through Docker instead? PHP is not on your host PATH, so `bin/weld.ps1 up` and `bin/weld.sh up` run the same install inside the app container for you (skip it with `--no-advisor`, or `-NoAdvisor` on Windows); see ADVISOR's README for the details.

### Clone it and rename

Want an app that is yours instead of a copy of WELD? Clone it, rename the four things that still say WELD, give it its own key, and re-run the checks.

Clone into a folder named for the new app:

```
git clone https://github.com/waynestate/weld.git my-app
cd my-app
```

Rename these four things:

| What | Where | Change |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Composer name | `composer.json`, the `"name"` field | `waynestate/weld` becomes your package, e.g. `wayne-state/my-app` |
| App name | `.env.example` (and `.env` once you have one) | `APP_NAME=WELD` becomes your app name; `VITE_APP_NAME` follows it through `${APP_NAME}` |
| Site title | `site/index.html`, the `` tag | `WELD: Many parts, one piece.` becomes yours; the front page copy is about WELD itself, so rewrite it for your app |
| Git remote | repository config | point `origin` at your own repository |

The `App\` namespace stays as it is; nothing in the app, the tests or the welded packages needs it renamed.

Then give the copy its own key and remote. Skip the copy if `up` already made `.env`. Windows PowerShell:

```powershell
Copy-Item .env.example .env
php artisan key:generate
git remote set-url origin https://git.example.com/you/my-app.git
```

macOS and Linux (sh):

```sh
cp .env.example .env
php artisan key:generate
git remote set-url origin https://git.example.com/you/my-app.git
```

Then re-run the checks the way CI does: `.\bin\weld.ps1 test` (or `bin/weld.sh test`), which runs `composer ci` in the container, plus `composer proctor` for the standards check. A photocopy is not a weld yet: when the checks pass under your name, the seam holds.

Want a smaller starting point than a full Laravel app? Sourdough is the starter tool for every shape of Wayne State app. It bakes four shapes today: raw PHP, Laravel with Blade, Laravel with Blade plus Vue islands, and Laravel with Inertia and Vue; only raw PHP with a Vue SPA is not available yet. WELD is the Inertia and Vue shape, already assembled with every part wired and ready to clone.

### What is welded in

| Part | What it does in WELD |
|---|---|
| WayneUI | The interface: Wayne State's design system, wired into the Vue front end and Blade layouts |
| CREED | The written standards and `policy.json`: supported PHP, Laravel and Node versions |
| Pinstripe | The coding standard: Pint, PHPStan level 8, ESLint and Prettier |
| Preflight | The CI pipeline, from GitLab CI/CD components |
| PROCTOR | The checks, run in CI and as the deploy gate |
| SESAME | Sign-in: CAS, Entra ID (OpenID Connect) and the auth gateway driver, and app-native sessions |
| HELMET | The baseline runtime: security headers and CSP, sessions, trusted proxies, `/up` |
| Ziggy | Route names as URLs: the route list ships inside the Vite bundle, so `route()` works in Vue without an inline script |

### Status

HELMET, SESAME and PROCTOR are welded in from Packagist; the rest of the cast is on Packagist too and gets welded on
in turn.
What is on the bench today:

- `composer.json` is `waynestate/weld`, requires PHP `^8.3`, and the lock file resolves for 8.3.0
- `.env.example` sets `APP_NAME=WELD`, `LOG_CHANNEL=stderr` and `SESSION_DRIVER=database`
- `Schema::defaultStringLength(191)` keeps index keys under Citadel's MySQL 5.6 767-byte cap
- `.gitattributes` sets `* text=auto eol=lf`
- `composer ci` is the CI contract: it runs validate, the tests with Pest, Pint, PHPStan level 8, the agent-ready check and audit, the
  same command on GitLab and GitHub
- `pint.json` and `phpstan.neon` still copy Pinstripe's 0.1 Laravel presets; Pinstripe 0.1.1 is on Packagist
  (tagged), and they switch to `includes: vendor/waynestate/pinstripe/...` when WELD requires it
- HELMET runs its security headers and CSP middleware in the global chain, so every response carries the baseline;
  the Vite build takes the per-request nonce; trusted proxies are a literal list in `bootstrap/app.php`; `/up` stays
  Laravel's built-in health route
- SESAME owns sign-in at `/login` and `/logout`; the fake driver stands in for the identity provider locally, and
  CAS is an env change away
- PROCTOR measures WELD against CREED's `policy.json` as a CI job (`composer proctor`): warnings pass, failures
  block
- The starter kit's password auth (register, login, password reset, two-factor) is removed on purpose; the door is
  SESAME's
- The license is MIT

**Testing.** Write new tests in Pest. Use an `it('...', function () { ... });` closure under `tests/Feature` or `tests/Unit`; the existing
PHPUnit class tests keep working and are converted only when you touch them. `composer test` runs both, and `tests/Pest.php` binds the
Feature tests to the Laravel app and a fresh database. The suite runs on a fixed dummy `APP_KEY` set in `phpunit.xml` so it boots with no
`.env`; the app refuses that key in production, so a copied test config cannot ship.

Best practices for building, running and deploying WELD live in [BEST_PRACTICES.md](https://nougat.snu.gs/enterprise-apps/weld/blob/HEAD/BEST_PRACTICES.md).

### Run it locally

One command strikes the spark; the containers do the welding. Docker is the only
prerequisite: PHP and Node run in the containers, so the host needs neither.

- Windows (PowerShell 5.1 or 7): `.\bin\weld.ps1 up`
- macOS / Linux: `bin/weld.sh up`

`up` copies `.env.example` to `.env` if it is missing, installs the PHP and Node
dependencies in the containers, starts the app and Vite, generates the app key if
it is not set, and runs the migrations. Then open http://localhost:8000.

The same subcommands work on every OS:

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `up` | Bring the whole stack up, as above |
| `down` | Stop and remove the containers |
| `test` | Run `composer ci` in the app container |
| `doctor` | Run `php artisan weld:doctor` in the app container |
| `logs` | Follow the container logs |

Deploying somewhere other than a laptop? [Running WELD off Citadel](https://nougat.snu.gs/enterprise-apps/weld/blob/HEAD/docs/running-off-citadel.md) covers OpenShift,
Coolify and plain Docker, with Citadel for comparison.

### Oracle

WELD speaks Oracle through `yajra/laravel-oci8`, and the wiring is already in: an `oracle` connection in
`config/database.php`, a check command, and plain-language sentences for the common errors. Until you set the
Oracle settings it stays dormant: nothing connects and nothing errors.

Fill in one set of names in `.env` (the commented block in `.env.example`): `ORACLE_USERNAME`, `ORACLE_PASSWORD`,
and either `ORACLE_TNS` (an Easy Connect string, `host:port/service`, or a full descriptor) or `ORACLE_HOST`,
`ORACLE_PORT` and `ORACLE_SERVICE_NAME`. On a server, set them in the app's environment settings, never in a file
in git.

Check the settings and the connection in plain language, one line per finding:

```
php artisan oracle:check
```

The local `app` container runs the stock Composer image, which has no Oracle driver. When you need a real
connection from your machine, the Oracle-ready image is opt-in through `compose.oracle.yaml`:

```
# Windows (PowerShell):
$env:WELD_ORACLE_IMAGE = "squire/oracle-parity:8.3"
docker compose -f compose.yaml -f compose.oracle.yaml up
# macOS / Linux:
WELD_ORACLE_IMAGE=squire/oracle-parity:8.3 docker compose -f compose.yaml -f compose.oracle.yaml up
```

The overlay swaps only the app's image and passes the `ORACLE_*` settings through from `.env`; the ports stay
bound to `127.0.0.1`. It fails closed when `WELD_ORACLE_IMAGE` is unset.

`squire/oracle-parity:8.3` is the name Squire documents for its parity image; build it once with Squire's
`scripts/oracle-image-build.sh --flavour parity --php 8.3` (the name is a placeholder until a registry is chosen).

### Check your setup

Maintainers: how to build, test and release this project, and where its data comes from, is in [MAINTAINING.md](https://nougat.snu.gs/enterprise-apps/weld/blob/HEAD/MAINTAINING.md).

`weld:doctor` strikes an arc across the local setup and reports every joint: the app key,
writable storage, the database and pending migrations. One line per check, PASS or WARN or FAIL;
exit code 1 when anything FAILs, so it works as a gate. The standards checks (PHP version, debug
in production, secure session cookies) belong to PROCTOR: run `composer proctor`, and the doctor
report says so. A good bead is a quiet one: all PASS and nothing to say.

- Windows (PowerShell): `.\bin\weld.ps1 doctor`
- macOS / Linux: `bin/weld.sh doctor`
- Straight to the container: `docker compose run --rm app php artisan weld:doctor`

Add `--json` to any of them for a machine-readable report.

### WELD and Sourdough

Sourdough is the starter tool for every shape of Wayne State app. It bakes four shapes today: raw PHP, Laravel with Blade, Laravel with Blade plus Vue islands, and Laravel with Inertia and Vue; only raw PHP with a Vue SPA is not available yet.
WELD is one of those shapes, Laravel with Inertia and Vue, with every part already joined and proved to work together.
Pick Sourdough when you want a starter you shape yourself. Pick WELD when you want the finished piece.

### Is WELD still Sourdough's Inertia shape?

Sourdough writes a manifest of every file it generates (`.sourdough/manifest.json`: each path with its SHA-256).
`bin/regen-check.php` compares that manifest with WELD file by file, skipping the product files WELD adds on top
(listed in `.sourdough/product-files.json`) and any path with a `vendor` or `node_modules` segment. Each remaining
path is reported as IDENTICAL, DIFFERS, MISSING_IN_WELD or RELOCATED.

Sourdough keeps Squire's deploy kit at the app root, and WELD keeps it under `deploy/`; the gate reports those
files as relocated, not drift, when the `deploy/` copy is byte-identical. `php artisan oracle:check` finds the
check file in either place.

The gate is a ratchet: `.sourdough/regen-baseline.json` records the drift already known and accepted, and the check
fails only on new drift. CI runs it against a fresh `sourdough new --inertia` generation from Sourdough's main;
locally, point it at your own generation:

- Run the check: `php bin/regen-check.php --generated ` (or `composer regen-check -- --generated `)
- Record the current drift as accepted: add `--write-baseline`

The Wayne State app stack

## WELD

WELD stands for Wired, Everything, Linked, Deployed.

Many parts, one piece.

WELD is a Laravel 13 app with Inertia and Vue, and the rest of the stack is already in it: sign-in, security headers, the standards check, code style, CI and WayneUI. It's **one install**. Rename it and start on your own pages.

`$ composer create-project waynestate/weld my-app`

Any other shape? [Sourdough](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/) starts four of the five, from raw PHP to Vue islands, with the same sign-in, headers and checks.

[Get started](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/#start) [Which piece do I need?](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/#chooser) [Meet the cast](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/#cast-title) [Docs](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/index.html)

Start here

### Install it, then run one command

Yes, this is a lot of packages. Most of you can ignore that. Install WELD, run the one command in step 2, and you have a working app with all of it set up. We split the stack into separate projects because Wayne State developers work on very different apps, and you shouldn't have to buy the whole shop to borrow one torch.

1. ### Install
   Composer makes a fresh copy, writes `.env`, sets the app key and runs the first migration.
   ```
   composer create-project waynestate/weld my-app
   ```
2. ### Start it in Docker
   This is the one command. You only need Docker, because PHP and Node run in the containers. Then open `localhost:8000`.
   ```
   # macOS, Linux
   bin/weld.sh up
   # Windows (PowerShell)
   .\bin\weld.ps1 up
   ```
3. ### Run the checks
   Runs the tests, Pint, PHPStan and `composer audit`, the same command CI runs. The standards check is separate: `composer proctor`.
   ```
   composer ci
   ```

[Sourdough](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/) makes the other shapes: `sourdough new my-app` for raw PHP, `sourdough new my-app --laravel` for Laravel with Blade, `sourdough new my-app --laravel --vue` for Vue islands. WELD is the Inertia and Vue shape, ready-made.

Already have an app?

### Which piece do I need?

Most Wayne State apps are older than this stack. Some are raw PHP, some are Laravel, and plenty only need sign-in or an upgrade. That's why every piece also works on its own. WELD is simply all of them installed together.

- I'm starting a new app
  WELD or [Sourdough](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/)
  Pick WELD for Laravel with Inertia and Vue, ready-made. Pick Sourdough to start any other shape, or to shape one yourself.
- My raw PHP app just needs sign-in
  [SESAME](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/)
  Adds CAS or Entra ID sign-in to a raw PHP or Laravel app. Your app keeps its own session.
- I'm stuck on PHP 7
  [Booster](https://booster.apps.wayne.edu/)
  Upgrades PHP and Laravel one version at a time, and has a playbook for Vue 2 to 3. It never commits; you read the diff and merge it.
- I'm deploying to Citadel
  [Squire](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/)
  The build and release scripts Citadel expects, a health check, and a way to run your app locally on the same images.
- I want CI on every push
  [Preflight](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/)
  GitLab CI components for PHP tests on each supported version, PROCTOR, Composer audit, Pint, PHPStan and ESLint.
- I want safe defaults at runtime
  [HELMET](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/)
  Sends the security headers and CSP, hardens the session cookie and checks proxies before your first page is served.
- I want it to look like Wayne State
  [WayneUI](https://wayneui.apps.wayne.edu/)
  Wayne State's design system. It works in static HTML, raw PHP, Blade and Vue.
- I want Citadel to sign people in before my app
  [Drawbridge](https://drawbridge.apps.wayne.edu/)
  A gateway that signs people in through Entra ID before they reach your app. Your app then checks one small signed token.
- I look after a lot of apps
  [Rollcall](https://rollcall.apps.wayne.edu/)
  Scans your apps and reports which PHP, Laravel and sign-in package each one runs, checked against CREED's support dates.
- I code with an AI agent
  [ADVISOR](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/)
  An MCP server your agent can ask about the stack. It answers from CREED's policy file, not from what the model remembers.

#### How the four check projects fit together

CREED writes the rules down and PROCTOR grades your app against them. Pinstripe is the code style. Preflight runs all of it in CI.

1. [CREED](https://creed.apps.wayne.edu/) the rules
   The written standards, plus `policy.json`: which PHP, Laravel and Node versions are supported.
2. [PROCTOR](https://proctor.apps.wayne.edu/) the grader
   Reads your `composer.json` and lock file and reports each check against CREED as pass, warning, info or fail.
3. [Pinstripe](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/) the code style
   Shared presets for Pint, PHPStan, Rector, ESLint and Prettier. Your app adds only its own exceptions.
4. [Preflight](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/) the runner
   The CI pipeline that runs all of it, and your tests, on every push.

WELD already has all four set up. Run `composer ci` and `composer proctor` on your machine, and GitLab runs both through Preflight on every push.

### The journey

Roughly in order: what happens to a request on its way to the page, then what happens to your code before it ships.

1. [HELMET](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/) sets security headers
2. [SESAME](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/) signs the user in
3. [WayneUI](https://wayneui.apps.wayne.edu/) renders the page
4. [PROCTOR](https://proctor.apps.wayne.edu/) checks the code
5. [Preflight](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/) runs CI
6. [Squire](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/) deploys

Up close

### The cast

The same projects with a bit more detail. The first seven are part of WELD. The next five work around your app: upgrades, the fleet scan, deploys, the sign-in gateway and the MCP server. After those come Sourdough and the one we're building next.

![WayneUI logo: a rounded frame around a solid shape, with a gold tab on the lower edge](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/assets/marks/wayneui.svg)

#### [WayneUI](https://wayneui.apps.wayne.edu/)

2.0 Contrast | AA

Wayne State's design system. WELD uses it in the Vue front end and the Blade layouts.

```
$ pnpm verify
✓ tokens     built
✓ contrast   AA, every pair
✓ axe        0 violations
a11y: 100
$
```

![CREED logo: a stone arch with a gold keystone](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/assets/marks/creed.png)

#### [CREED](https://creed.apps.wayne.edu/)

0.1 Volume | Eleven

The written standards, plus `policy.json` with the support dates for PHP, Laravel, Node, MySQL, Vue and Inertia. PROCTOR, Rollcall and ADVISOR all read it.

```
$ creed policy show
php      8.3, 8.4
laravel  12, 13
node     22 LTS
volume   eleven
$
```

![HELMET logo: a white football helmet with a gold facemask](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/assets/marks/helmet.png)

#### [HELMET](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/)

0.2 Fit | Snug

In WELD it runs in the global middleware, so every response carries the security headers and CSP.

```
$ helmet headers
CSP      strict, nonce
HSTS     1 year
frames   DENY
$
```

![SESAME logo: an open door with a gold gap](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/assets/marks/sesame.png)

#### [SESAME](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/)

0.2 Says | Open

Sign-in through CAS, Entra ID or Drawbridge. Locally, a fake driver signs you in.

```
$ sesame login
→ off to CAS and back
✓ signed in as ab1234
✓ session: app-native
$
```

![PROCTOR logo: an eye with a gold square pupil](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/assets/marks/proctor.png)

#### [PROCTOR](https://proctor.apps.wayne.edu/)

0.2 Strictness | Kind

In WELD it's `composer proctor`. In CI, warnings pass and failures block.

```
$ proctor check
✓ php 8.4 supported
✓ headers present
✓ 42 passed, 0 failed
$
```

![Preflight logo: a runway with a gold center line](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/assets/marks/preflight.png)

#### [Preflight](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/)

0.1 Checklist | Long

GitLab CI/CD components. WELD's pipeline uses them to run the tests on PHP 8.3, 8.4 and 8.5, plus the audit.

```
$ preflight run
✓ lint         pass
✓ test         312 pass
✓ portability  pass
$
```

![Pinstripe logo: a striped necktie with a gold tie bar](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/assets/marks/pinstripe.png)

#### [Pinstripe](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/)

0.1 Creases | Sharp

The code style presets. WELD runs Pint and PHPStan at level 8 from a copy of Pinstripe's 0.1 Laravel presets.

```
$ pinstripe apply
✓ pint      14 files pressed
✓ phpstan   level 8, 0 errors
✓ eslint    clean
style: sharp
$
```

![Booster logo: a syringe with rocket fins and a gold flame](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/assets/marks/booster.png)

#### [Booster](https://booster.apps.wayne.edu/)

0.1 Sting | Mild

Plans an upgrade as hops, like Laravel 10 to 11, and runs them one at a time with Rector. Your tests have to pass on the new PHP before the next hop starts.

```
$ booster plan
1. laravel-10-to-11
2. laravel-11-to-12
3. php-82-to-83
$
```

![Rollcall logo: an open register with gold ticks](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/assets/marks/rollcall.png)

#### [Rollcall](https://rollcall.apps.wayne.edu/)

0.1 Attendance | Taken

Every app answers “present”, with its PHP, Laravel and auth versions. Rollcall only reports. It never opens an issue or blocks a deploy.

```
$ rollcall report
✓ snapshot   today
drift      none
back row   PHP 7.4, waving
$
```

![Squire logo: a satchel with a gold buckle](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/assets/marks/squire.png)

#### [Squire](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/)

0.3 Armor | Carried

The deploy kit for Citadel: `build.sh`, a release script, a health check and local runs on the same images. This page deploys with it too.

```
$ squire doctor
✓ build.sh     packages only
✓ release.sh   idempotent
✓ /up          answers
$
```

![Drawbridge logo: a castle tower with its bridge down on a gold chain](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/assets/marks/drawbridge.png)

#### [Drawbridge](https://drawbridge.apps.wayne.edu/)

0.1 Moat | Full

One OpenID Connect client, through Entra ID, for every app on Citadel. We'd rather get the nonce and state checks right once than in every app.

```
$ drawbridge config:validate
✓ oidc        Entra ID, PKCE
✓ protected   /admin/
✓ headers     stripped, every spelling
bridge: lowered
$
```

![ADVISOR logo: a speech bubble with a gold compass needle](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/assets/marks/advisor.png)

#### [ADVISOR](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/)

0.1 Office hours | Always

Ask it which PHP you can build on and it answers from `policy.json`, with the date. It's read-only in 0.1: it can't write files or run shell commands.

```
$ advisor mcp
✓ serving   stdio
✓ tools     read-only
answers: from policy.json
$
```

![Sourdough logo: a starter jar with a gold band](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/assets/marks/sourdough.png)

#### [Sourdough](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/)

0.1 Rise | Daily

`sourdough new` makes a new app with SESAME, HELMET, PROCTOR and Preflight already in place. Use it when you'd rather shape the app yourself. It bakes four of the five app shapes today, and it is the starter for every shape.

```
$ sourdough new --raw
Next steps:
  cd my-app
  composer install
$
```

#### Next off the line

- Rolodex next
  Person data with types, so nobody has to flip through cards by hand.

### Pick your path

The stack has five app shapes. Sourdough bakes four of them today; only raw PHP with a Vue SPA is still waiting. WELD is the Inertia and Vue one, built.

From Sourdough

#### Raw PHP

Plain PHP with no framework and no build step, using WayneUI's standalone files.

`composer global require waynestate/sourdough sourdough new my-app --raw`

From Sourdough

#### Laravel + Blade

Laravel with Blade views, the classic WSU shape.

`sourdough new my-app --laravel`

From Sourdough

#### Laravel + Blade + Vue islands

Laravel with Blade views, and a little Vue where a page needs behavior.

`sourdough new my-app --laravel --vue`

This is WELD

#### Laravel + Inertia/Vue

Laravel 13 with Inertia 2 and Vue 3. This is the shape WELD is, with the stack already installed.

`composer create-project waynestate/weld my-app`

Not baked yet: raw PHP + Vue SPA (`--raw --vue`); it prints a plan today.

Hand it to your agent

### Job tickets

Two prompts for whatever coding agent you use. Copy one, or open it in OpenCode, Claude Code, Codex or ChatGPT. Each tells the agent what's already set up and what it must leave alone, and both tell it to ask you before it guesses.

#### Get started with WELD

Gets a new app running in Docker, checks it, and plans the rename. It won't rename anything until you say so.

A prompt for your coding agent. Copy it as it stands:

```text
You are a coding agent helping a Wayne State University developer start a new app from WELD: the Wayne State application stack welded into one Laravel app with Inertia and Vue. Sign-in (SESAME), security headers (HELMET), the standards check (PROCTOR) and CI are already joined. The job is to get it running and make it this developer's own.

Read first:
- https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/llms.txt, the index of WELD's pages, each one as Markdown. Fetch the pages you need; do not work from memory.
- ADVISOR, the stack's MCP server, if it is connected: get_project_status and read_project_docs for weld answer from the stack's own docs, and policy_lookup gives today's PHP, Laravel and Node support from CREED. If it is not connected, say so and work from the pages. How to add it: https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/llms.txt

Task:
1. Clone WELD into a new folder with `git clone https://github.com/waynestate/weld.git my-app`, using the app name I give you in place of my-app.
2. Bring it up with Docker, the only prerequisite: `.\bin\weld.ps1 up` on Windows (PowerShell), `bin/weld.sh up` on macOS and Linux. It copies .env.example to .env, installs the PHP and Node dependencies in the containers, sets the app key and runs the migrations.
3. Check the setup with the doctor subcommand (`.\bin\weld.ps1 doctor` or `bin/weld.sh doctor`) and report every line that is not PASS.
4. Run the gate with the test subcommand, which runs `composer ci` in the app container, and the standards check with `composer proctor` (in the app container if the host has no PHP).
5. Propose what to rename to make it mine: APP_NAME in .env.example and the package name in composer.json. Do not change them yet.

Constraints:
- WELD is Laravel with Inertia and Vue. If I want raw PHP or Laravel with Blade, stop and point me at Sourdough, the starter for every shape: https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/llms.txt
- Sign-in is SESAME's, at /login and /logout, and its fake driver stands in locally. Never add password auth back.
- Never commit .env, and never paste a secret into a prompt or a file.
- Give separate commands for Windows (PowerShell), macOS and Linux wherever they differ.
- Ask me before you guess: an app name, a check that fails for a reason you cannot explain, or anything that touches a deploy.

Output: what you ran and what it said, the doctor report, then the rename plan as numbered steps, then your questions.
```

#### Add a signed-in page to a WELD app

Adds a route behind SESAME, a Vue page in the app layout and a feature test, then runs the checks.

A prompt for your coding agent. Copy it as it stands:

```text
You are a coding agent adding one signed-in page to an app built from WELD: the Wayne State application stack welded into one Laravel app with Inertia and Vue, at Wayne State University.

Read first:
- https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/llms.txt, then the pages it lists. BEST_PRACTICES.md in this repo says what each practice expects and which stack tool checks it.
- ADVISOR, the stack's MCP server, if it is connected: call list_stack_rules with permutation laravel-inertia-vue, and read_project_docs for weld and sesame. If it is not connected, say so and work from the pages.
- routes/web.php, resources/js/pages/Dashboard.vue, resources/js/layouts/ and tests/Feature/DashboardTest.php.

Task:
1. If I have not said what the page is for, its URL and who may see it, ask.
2. Add the route in routes/web.php the way the dashboard route does it: Inertia::render for a page in resources/js/pages, behind the auth.sesame middleware, with a route name.
3. Write the Vue page with script setup and TypeScript, inside AppLayout with breadcrumbs, the way Dashboard.vue does.
4. Add a feature test beside DashboardTest.php: a guest is sent to /login, and a user signed in with the fake driver gets the page.
5. Run the gate: `composer ci`, or the test subcommand of bin/weld.sh (macOS, Linux) or bin\weld.ps1 (Windows) when the host has no PHP.

Constraints:
- Sign-in belongs to SESAME: protect the route with auth.sesame, and never add password auth.
- HELMET sends a strict CSP with a per-request nonce: no inline scripts, and no new script hosts.
- Keep PHPStan at level 8 and Pint clean. Never lower either to get the gate green.
- Ask me before you guess, and before you add a migration, a Composer or npm package, or anything that touches a deploy.

Output: the files you changed, the gate's result, then your questions.
```

The agent reads the same pages you do: [llms.txt](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/llms.txt) lists them, [llms-full.txt](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/llms-full.txt) holds them all in one file, and this page has a [Markdown twin](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/index.md). Nothing here phones home. The buttons only copy text or open the tool you picked.

---

Source: https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/changelog.html

## Changelog | WELD docs

Notable changes to WELD, newest first.

### Unreleased[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/changelog.html#unreleased)

- Changed: the front page header has a main nav that includes Docs.
- Changed: the test APP_KEY is an obvious dummy (32 zero bytes), labeled test-only, and `App\Support\DummyAppKey` makes the app refuse it when `APP_ENV=production`; tests cover both.
- Changed: the regen gate treats Squire kit files that WELD keeps under `deploy/` as relocated (not drift), and `oracle:check` finds the check file at the app root or under `deploy/`.
- Changed: WELD adopts Pest 4 for new tests: the PHPUnit class tests run unchanged, `composer test` runs Pest over the whole suite, `tests/Pest.php` is configured, the example feature test is converted, and `pestphp/pest` is required at `^4` because Pest 5 needs PHP 8.4.
- Changed: CI pins the Preflight components to the 0.1.4 release SHA, so PROCTOR's preflight-pinned check passes.
- Changed: the GitHub Actions in WELD's CI (`actions/checkout`, `shivammathur/setup-php`) are pinned to commit SHAs with the tag in a comment, so PROCTOR's `ci-pipelines-unpinned-uses` warning is gone; setup-php moves from the unpublished `@v3` to 2.40.0.
- Added: a docs site (site/docs/) built by the shared docs builder from docs/, checked in composer ci.
- Changed: the regeneration baseline shrinks from 66 to 62 known-drift paths now that Sourdough no longer ships `resources/js/app.js`, `welcome.blade.php` or a phantom `vite.config.js`, and the `.editorconfig` matches.
- Fixed: `npm run lint` passes on the shipped code: the dead `badgeDir` constant leaves `scripts/readme-art/build.mjs`, and Squire's kit bytes (`site/assets/agent-ready.js`, `site/assets/stack-env.js`, with the unused `catch (e)` bindings and dead variables fixed in Squire's kit) are synced in, so the ESLint config no longer excludes them.
- Changed: `npm run lint` is now a pure check (`eslint .`); a new `npm run fix` script runs `eslint . --fix`.
- Fixed: TrustedProxiesTest no longer depends on a local .env file. The trustProxies() closure in bootstrap/app.php runs when the HTTP kernel resolves on the first request, after the test's app refresh has re-read .env into the process environment, so the .env that composer create-project writes clobbered the value the test set and one of the four tests failed. The helper now re-asserts TRUSTED_PROXIES after the refresh, so the suite is green with a .env present and without one.
- Changed: the README and front page say Sourdough bakes four shapes today (raw PHP, Laravel with Blade, Laravel with Blade plus Vue islands, and Laravel with Inertia and Vue) and only raw PHP with a Vue SPA is not available yet; the front page gains a card for the islands shape. WELD is the Inertia and Vue shape, already assembled with every part wired.
- Changed: the front-page deploy layer pins HELMET ^0.3, PROCTOR ^0.4 and CREED ^0.1 (lock: HELMET 0.3.0, PROCTOR 0.4.0, CREED 0.1.6).
- Changed: CI pins Preflight 0.1.4 (GitLab component includes and the GitHub reusable workflow at its tag commit); the deploy layer sets minimum-stability to stable.
- Changed: HELMET moves to ^0.3 and PROCTOR to ^0.4 (lock: HELMET 0.3.0, PROCTOR 0.4.x, CREED 0.1.6, ADVISOR 0.1.5), so the newest PROCTOR checks run on WELD itself; an empty `HELMET_PROXIES=` now trusts nobody. Tests, style, analysis and PROCTOR pass unchanged.

### 0.1.2 (2026-11-03)[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/changelog.html#0-1-2-2026-11-03)

- Changed: SESAME moves from 0.2 to 0.4 (`^0.4`). It now logs sign-in events (`sesame.login`, `sesame.logout`, with a per sign-in `session_ref`; turn off with `SESAME_LOG=false`), re-reads the signed-in user when the resolver asks for it, and the gateway driver refuses an `at+jwt` access token. WELD itself needed no code change.
- Fixed: the user menu gains a Sign out item on SESAME's logout route, the app bar branding drops the Laravel Starter Kit name and links (WELD logo text, waynestate/weld repository, weld.apps.wayne.edu documentation), .editorconfig covers compose.yaml and its variants, ExampleTest stops booting the framework, and UiBrandingTest pins the branding.
- Changed: docs and package metadata name nougat as the canonical repository, with git.wayne.edu and GitHub as read-only mirrors, until git.wayne.edu has CI runners.
- Changed: Laravel's trusted proxy list now comes from the TRUSTED_PROXIES environment variable (unset keeps Citadel's 172.18.0.1, set but empty trusts none, `*` trusts all), instead of a literal address. Citadel behaviour is unchanged.
- Changed: the README and front page now say Sourdough is the starter tool for every shape of Wayne State app (raw PHP and Laravel with Blade today, the Vue shapes planned) and WELD is the Inertia and Vue shape, already assembled and ready to clone.
- Changed: CI pulls its Docker Hub images through the GitLab Dependency Proxy (the group's CI_DEPENDENCY_PROXY_GROUP_IMAGE_PREFIX), so pipelines no longer hit Docker Hub's anonymous pull limit.
- Added: `waynestate/advisor` joins `require-dev` at `^0.1`, and "Clone it and rename" gains one step: `php vendor/bin/advisor install --client=claude --write` writes `.mcp.json`, which is now git-ignored because a committed MCP config would run a program on whoever opens the project. Set `ADVISOR_ENABLED=1` in `.env` to switch the advisor on.
- Changed: `bin/weld.ps1 up` and `bin/weld.sh up` write `.mcp.json` from ADVISOR inside the app container as part of the first-run setup (no PHP on the host PATH in the Docker path), with a `--no-advisor` opt-out on both scripts (`-NoAdvisor` on the PowerShell one).
- Changed: the deploy layer's Squire kit is refreshed to 0.3.3 (release options can now live in ./.env.squire).
- Changed: the deploy layer's Squire kit is refreshed to 0.3.4 (the local .env.squire file is now git-ignored).
- Changed: the deploy layer's Squire kit is refreshed to 0.4.0: deploy/oracle-check.php arrives, so `php artisan oracle:check` runs the real check, and release.sh runs it without failing the release.
- Changed: the Oracle overlay docs name Squire's parity image, `squire/oracle-parity:8.3`.
- Added: `StackIntegrationTest` pins HELMET's security headers on a signed-in dashboard, a 404 error page and `/up`; `ProctorCheckTest` runs PROCTOR against CREED's policy.json inside the test suite, which `composer ci` alone did not cover.
- Added: README section "Clone it and rename": copy WELD, rename the composer name, APP_NAME, site title and git remote, regenerate the key and re-run the checks, for PowerShell and sh.
- Changed: BEST_PRACTICES.md re-checked against the code on 2026-11-02: the Squire kit's Dockerfile, entrypoint and release script move W10, W12, W16 and W24 from `Not yet` to `Documented`, W8/W13/W22 sentences name the new deploy files, and the shifted line numbers in composer.json, .env.example and bootstrap/app.php are corrected.
- Added: the regen gate, which makes "WELD is the prebuilt Inertia shape" checkable: `bin/regen-check.php` compares a freshly generated Sourdough Inertia app (its `.sourdough/manifest.json`, path to SHA-256) with WELD file by file, skipping `.sourdough/product-files.json` entries and any `vendor` or `node_modules` path, and fails only on drift not already recorded in `.sourdough/regen-baseline.json` (a ratchet; `--write-baseline` records the current drift). The logic lives in `App\Support\RegenCheck` with unit tests, `composer regen-check` passes arguments through (not part of `ci`), and warning-only `regen-gate` jobs in both pipelines generate a fresh app from Sourdough's main and run the gate.

### 0.1.1 (2026-10-29)[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/changelog.html#0-1-1-2026-10-29)

- Added: agent-ready site (prompt blocks, Markdown twins, llms.txt), from Squire's kit.
- Fixed: stale capability claims in the site and docs.
- Changed: project names written as words except acronyms.
- `npm run typecheck` (vue-tsc, no emit) joins the scripts, and it passes: the ten errors from the first run are fixed in the bullets below.
- `site/assets/wayne-ui/marks/warrior-strong-reverse.svg` comes back from the WayneUI static bundle; the CSS has pointed at it since the front page assets landed.
- The tsconfig `types` array keeps `vite/client` and regains `./resources/js/types`: the shared interfaces move from `index.ts` to `index.d.ts`, which is the shape that entry resolves to. `vue/tsx` stays out, because it never resolved.
- `VITE_APP_NAME` is declared in a new `resources/js/env.d.ts` against vite/client's `ImportMetaEnv`, replacing the inline `declare module` block in the app entry.
- The app entry imports the Ziggy config from a new `ziggy-value.js` beside the generated `ziggy.js`, with a matching `ziggy-value.d.ts`: the generated declaration names the routes but not the value, and the value's string `location` predates the package's typed shape, so the declaration stops at the config minus that field.
- `SharedData` extends Inertia's `PageProps`, so it satisfies the constraint `usePage` puts on its type argument.
- AppHeader types its page with `usePage<SharedData>()`, so the user menu meets a `User` instead of `unknown`.
- TextLink's optional `method` prop takes Inertia's `Method` union instead of `string`.
- Welcome reads the signed-in state from `usePage<SharedData>()` instead of `$page`, which vue-tsc does not recognize on the component instance.

### 0.1.0 (2026-10-29)[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/changelog.html#0-1-0-2026-10-29)

- `waynestate/helmet` moves from `^0.1` to `^0.2` (locked at 0.2.3). The published `config/helmet.php` re-syncs with the package: `HELMET_PRESET` fills the proxy list (an unknown name throws at boot), and the security headers middleware joins the global chain, so every response carries the baseline. The trusted-header set narrows to `X-Forwarded-For` and `X-Forwarded-Proto`; `X-Forwarded-Port` is no longer trusted, because Citadel's HA-Proxy never sends it.
- `php artisan weld:doctor`: local setup only: the app key, writable storage, the database and pending migrations. The standards checks (PHP version, debug in production, secure session cookies) belong to PROCTOR, and the report points at `composer proctor`.
- Ziggy's route list leaves the inline `<script>` from `@routes` and moves into the Vite bundle: `composer ziggy` generates `resources/js/ziggy.js` (plus `ziggy.d.ts`), the app entry imports it and passes it to `ZiggyVue`, so `route()` works in Vue exactly as before while HELMET's strict CSP stays closed. A CI job regenerates the file and fails on any diff, and a feature test pins the contract that every script tag on the app page carries a nonce.
- PROCTOR is welded in from Packagist (`waynestate/proctor` dev dependency, CREED's `policy.json` carried by `waynestate/creed`): `composer proctor` measures WELD against the version policy, and a CI job runs it on every pipeline. Warnings pass, failures block. The package's own bin looks for its autoloader where only a project-root install puts one, so `composer proctor` runs directly without a temporary launcher.
- SESAME is welded in from Packagist (`waynestate/sesame`): sign-in moves from the starter kit's password forms to `/login` and `/logout`, owned by the package. The fake driver signs in locally; pointing at CAS is an env change. A `username` column joins `users`, and `App\Sesame\UserResolver` imports the identity on first sign-in.
- HELMET is welded in from Packagist (`waynestate/helmet`): security headers and CSP on every web response, a published `config/helmet.php`, trusted proxies in `bootstrap/app.php`, and the Vite build asks for the per-request nonce. `/up` stays Laravel's built-in health route. Every web response now wears the baseline.
- `docs/running-off-citadel.md`: the off-Citadel contract: OpenShift, Coolify and plain Docker, with Citadel for comparison. Traffic and trusted proxies per platform, `php://stderr` logs, writable paths, non-root user, `/up`, and `weld:doctor` after every deploy. Same bead, four different tables.
- README: one line under "Run it locally" linking the guide.
- `php artisan weld:doctor`: checks the app is set up safely, one PASS, WARN or FAIL line per check (PHP version, app key, debug in production, secure session cookies, writable storage, database, pending migrations); exits 1 when anything FAILs, `--json` for machines. A good bead is a quiet one: all PASS and nothing to say.
- `bin/weld.ps1` and `bin/weld.sh`: a `doctor` subcommand runs it in the app container.
- README: "Check your setup".
- `compose.yaml`: the local stack: the app (PHP and Composer in one image) and Vite, on pinned images, SQLite per `.env.example`, ports bound to 127.0.0.1 only.
- `bin/weld.ps1` (Windows, PowerShell 5.1 and 7) and `bin/weld.sh` (Linux and macOS, POSIX sh): `up`, `down`, `test` and `logs`, the same subcommands on every OS.
- README: "Run it locally" is now one command per OS.

## Contributing[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/contributing.html#contributing)

This page tells you how to build, test, keep current and release WELD, and where each piece of work belongs.

### Where it lives[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/contributing.html#where-it-lives)

Development happens on nougat, the canonical repository: [enterprise-apps/weld](https://nougat.snu.gs/enterprise-apps/weld). The GitHub repository and git.wayne.edu are read-only mirrors: `main` and tags are copied automatically. Changes, issues and merge requests go to nougat. Nobody pushes to the mirrors.

Note

This moves to git.wayne.edu once it has CI runners. The weld is made on nougat; the mirrors only get the polished bead.

### Build and test[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/contributing.html#build-and-test)

The Docker path installs, migrates and serves in one command:

```sh
bin/weld.sh up
```

```powershell
.\bin\weld.ps1 up
```

All checks run `composer ci` in the container:

```sh
bin/weld.sh test
```

```powershell
.\bin\weld.ps1 test
```

Check your setup:

```sh
bin/weld.sh doctor
```

```powershell
.\bin\weld.ps1 doctor
```

Logs and stop:

```sh
bin/weld.sh logs
bin/weld.sh down
```

```powershell
.\bin\weld.ps1 logs
.\bin\weld.ps1 down
```

Without Docker: run `composer install`, `npm ci`, copy `.env.example` to `.env`, `php artisan key:generate`, then `composer ci`.

#### Other checks[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/contributing.html#other-checks)

| Check | Command |
| --- | --- |
| PROCTOR against CREED's policy | `composer proctor` |
| Ziggy routes are current | `composer ziggy`, then `git diff --exit-code resources/js/ziggy.*` |
| JS lint and format | `npm run lint` (pure check), `npm run fix` (apply fixes), `npm run format:check` |
| Production assets | `npm run build` |

`composer ci` runs `composer validate --strict`, the tests, Pint, PHPStan and `composer audit`. It does not run PROCTOR, Ziggy or the JS lint.

The regen gate checks that WELD is still Sourdough's Inertia shape. Generate a fresh app (`sourdough new <dir> --inertia`), then `php bin/regen-check.php --generated <dir>` (or `composer regen-check -- --generated <dir>`). It skips the product files listed in `.sourdough/product-files.json` and any `vendor` or `node_modules` path, and fails only on drift that is not already recorded in `.sourdough/regen-baseline.json`; `--write-baseline` records the current drift as accepted. It is not part of `composer ci`; CI runs it as a separate, warning-only job.

Pint skips `deploy/`. That folder is the stack's shared front-page deploy layer (Squire kit plus HELMET front controller), kept byte-identical in PER style across every stack repo, so WELD's Laravel preset must not reformat it. Its style is checked where it is made.

### CI[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/contributing.html#ci)

- **GitLab:** Preflight's `php-test` (PHP 8.3, 8.4, 8.5) and `composer-audit` components, a `composer-ci` job, a `proctor` job (warnings pass, failures block), a `ziggy` drift job and a `regen-gate` job (warning-only until `.sourdough/regen-baseline.json` is filled in).
- **GitHub:** `.github/workflows/ci.yml` calls Preflight's reusable workflow with `composer ci` and runs the same `regen-gate` check (`continue-on-error` until the baseline is filled in).

Green means all of those pass; the regen gate may warn while its baseline is being filled in. JS lint is not in CI yet.

### Keeping the joints current[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/contributing.html#keeping-the-joints-current)

- When HELMET, SESAME, CREED or PROCTOR release, raise the constraint here (`composer require waynestate/<part>:^0.x`), run all the checks above, and commit the lock file.
- When Laravel, Inertia or Vue release, Booster's hops are the way to move; WELD is a good first test for them.
- After route changes, regenerate Ziggy and commit the result.
- When Sourdough changes what it generates, the regen gate flags the new drift in CI. Fix it here or upstream in Sourdough; if the drift is accepted as intended, record it with `--write-baseline` and commit `.sourdough/regen-baseline.json`.

### Releasing[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/contributing.html#releasing)

WELD has no tags yet. When it gets one:

1. Move the lines under `## Unreleased` in `CHANGELOG.md` to a new `## X.Y.Z (YYYY-MM-DD)` heading.
2. All the checks above green locally, then both pipelines green for that commit.
3. Run a secrets scan of the history and check that nothing internal (server names, people, IDs) is in the tree.
4. Tag `X.Y.Z` (no `v`) on nougat. The mirror carries the tag to GitHub.
5. A release needs a maintainer's approval. Never move or delete a published tag.

### Running it elsewhere[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/contributing.html#running-it-elsewhere)

WELD targets Citadel first. [Running WELD off Citadel](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/running-off-citadel.html) covers OpenShift, Coolify and plain Docker, with Citadel for comparison.

### The front page[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/contributing.html#the-front-page)

`site/` is the stack's front page, for `https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/` on Citadel, served through a small raw-PHP `deploy/` layer generated with Squire (separate from the WELD app itself).

### The docs site[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/contributing.html#the-docs-site)

The docs site is built from `docs/` by the shared docs builder (`composer docs`) and checked by `composer docs:check`. Sources live in `docs/`; the page you read is the page that ships: same source, same bead.

### Related[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/contributing.html#related)

- [Running WELD off Citadel](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/running-off-citadel.html)

---

Source: https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/app-structure.html

## App structure[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/app-structure.html#app-structure)

This page lists the app structure practices for WELD, from the BEST_PRACTICES guide, with the tag that says whether the stack holds each one today.

### W1. One owner of authentication: SESAME[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/app-structure.html#w1-one-owner-of-authentication-sesame)

**Practice:** Remove the Laravel starter kit's Fortify routes and actions (`/login`, `/register`, `/forgot-password`, 2FA). SESAME's `findOrImportUser(Identity)` is the only way in.

**Why:** Two login systems mean two session rules and two audit trails, and the kit's Fortify registers its routes automatically.

**Stack:** `Documented`. SESAME is a dependency (`composer.json`), the starter kit's Fortify routes are removed, and `tests/Feature/AuthRoutesTest.php` fails if WELD grows its own auth routes. Target `Checked`: a PROCTOR check and a feature test over `php artisan route:list --json`.

### W2. WayneUI is the only component source[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/app-structure.html#w2-wayneui-is-the-only-component-source)

**Practice:** Pages use WayneUI components and tokens. Do not keep the kit's shadcn-vue components or Tailwind theme as a second design system.

**Why:** The stack's promise is one interface contract on every consumer path; a parallel component set breaks the accessibility gate.

**Stack:** `Not yet`. The shadcn-vue components and their npm dependencies are gone, but WayneUI is not wired in: the Vue components carry `TODO(wayneui)` stand-ins (for example `resources/js/layouts/settings/Layout.vue` and `resources/js/pages/settings/Profile.vue`) because WELD does not load WayneUI's stylesheet yet, and the Tailwind theme (`tailwind.config.js`) plus `cn()`/`clsx`/`tailwind-merge` (`resources/js/lib/utils.ts`, `package.json`) remain. Target `Checked`: an ESLint rule (Pinstripe) bans imports from the kit's `components/ui` path, and a check fails when `components.json` exists.

### W3. Own the app code; take stack changes through `sourdough feed` [#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/app-structure.html#w3-own-the-app-code-take-stack-changes-through-sourdough-feed)

**Practice:** The kit gives you the code ("full ownership"), with no kit upgrade path. WELD's wiring files are marked and refreshed by `sourdough feed`, not hand-edited.

**Why:** Without a feed the app forks from the stack on day one and never gets fixes.

**Stack:** `Not yet`. Sourdough is not a dependency yet, so there is no feed to run. Target `Checked`: WELD's CI runs `sourdough feed` against each stack release and fails on drift.

### W4. Inertia 3 only; migrate off the removed APIs[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/app-structure.html#w4-inertia-3-only-migrate-off-the-removed-apis)

**Practice:** Use `@inertiajs/vue3` ^3 and `inertiajs/inertia-laravel` ^3. Do not import Axios, call `Inertia::lazy()` (use `Inertia::optional()`), read `data-page`, or `require()` Inertia packages.

**Why:** Inertia 3 removed all of these; code copied from older tutorials fails or half-works.

**Stack:** `Not yet`. WELD is on Inertia 2, not 3: `composer.json` pins `inertiajs/inertia-laravel: ^2.0` and `package.json` pins `@inertiajs/vue3: ^2.0.0-beta.3`. The removed APIs are not used (no `axios` dependency, no `Inertia::lazy`, no `data-page`), so the migration is a version bump, not a rewrite. Target `Checked`: ESLint `no-restricted-imports` for `axios`, a grep check for `Inertia::lazy`, and Composer constraints.

### W5. Commit `.ai/rules`; ignore what Boost regenerates[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/app-structure.html#w5-commit-ai-rules-ignore-what-boost-regenerates)

**Practice:** Laravel Boost is a `require-dev` package. Commit `.ai/rules/` (project rules). Ignore `.mcp.json`, `boost.json` and the generated block of `CLAUDE.md`/`AGENTS.md`. WELD's own conventions go in `.ai/guidelines/` and each stack package may ship `resources/boost/guidelines/core.blade.php` and `resources/boost/skills/*/SKILL.md`.

**Why:** Rules are shared team memory; generated files change with every `boost:update`.

**Stack:** `Not yet`. Boost is not a dependency and there is no `.ai/` directory yet. Target `Checked`: PROCTOR confirms the `.gitignore` entries and that `.ai/rules/` exists.

### W6. Sail is local development only[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/app-structure.html#w6-sail-is-local-development-only)

**Practice:** Sail's own description is "Laravel's default Docker development environment". It is not a production image and WELD never deploys it.

**Why:** Sail's runtime images carry dev tooling and a bash-script CLI.

**Stack:** `Documented`. `composer.json` keeps `laravel/sail` in `require-dev`, so it is a local tool, not a runtime dependency. Target `Checked`: PROCTOR flags `laravel/sail` outside `require-dev` and any `vendor/laravel/sail` path in a production Dockerfile.

### W7. The supported dev path is Compose driven by native scripts, not Sail[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/app-structure.html#w7-the-supported-dev-path-is-compose-driven-by-native-scripts-not-sail)

**Practice:** Sail runs on Windows "via WSL2". The stack rule is that Windows needs no bash and no WSL. Ship `weld.ps1` and `weld.sh` (or one PHP command) over a plain `compose.yaml`; Sail stays an unsupported convenience.

**Why:** Every developer OS gets its own native path.

**Stack:** `Documented`. `compose.yaml` and the `bin/weld.ps1` / `bin/weld.sh` pair exist. Target `Checked`: a pair-parity test.

### W8. One image, several process types[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/app-structure.html#w8-one-image-several-process-types)

**Practice:** Build one image. Run it as `web`, `worker` and `scheduler` by changing the command only (plus `ssr` when Inertia SSR is on). On Compose these are services; on OpenShift a Deployment, a Deployment and a CronJob.

**Why:** One build means one tested artifact, and the process types stay identical in code.

**Stack:** `Not yet`. A Dockerfile now exists (`deploy/.squire/Dockerfile`, a local mirror of the image Citadel generates), but it runs one process type only: `CMD ["apache2-foreground"]` (`deploy/.squire/Dockerfile`), with no worker or scheduler variant. Target `Checked`: Preflight portability boots the image with each command.

### How to read the tags[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/app-structure.html#how-to-read-the-tags)

Each practice ends with exactly one tag.

| Tag | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `Enforced` | WELD's code does it or refuses to run without it, and a test covers it. |
| `Checked` | PROCTOR or CI warns or fails. |
| `Documented` | Written down in the README or a config file, with no check behind it. |
| `Not yet` | A gap. |

### Related[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/app-structure.html#related)

- [The container contract](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/container-contract.html)
- [Queues and scheduling](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/queues-and-scheduling.html)
- [Running WELD off Citadel](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/running-off-citadel.html)

## Build and supply chain[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/build-and-supply-chain.html#build-and-supply-chain)

This page states WELD's build and supply chain practices, one per heading, each with the rule and the tag that shows whether the stack holds it today.

### W30: Support only PHP versions that are not end of life[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/build-and-supply-chain.html#w30-support-only-php-versions-that-are-not-end-of-life)

**Practice:** `composer.json` requires `php: ^8.3` with `config.platform.php` `8.3.0`. Tests run on 8.3, 8.4 and 8.5. Laravel 13 needs 8.3 or newer.

**Stack:** `Checked`. `composer.json` requires `php: ^8.3`, `composer.json` sets `config.platform.php` to `8.3.0`, and the CI matrix runs on 8.3, 8.4 and 8.5 (`.gitlab-ci.yml` and `.github/workflows/ci.yml`).

### W31: Keep dev tools inside the PHP floor[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/build-and-supply-chain.html#w31-keep-dev-tools-inside-the-php-floor)

**Practice:** Pest 5 requires PHP `^8.4`. On a `^8.3` floor use Pest 4 or PHPUnit and cap the constraint.

**Stack:** `Checked`. WELD uses PHPUnit, not Pest: `composer.json` pins `phpunit/phpunit: ^12.0`, and the CI matrix starts at 8.3 (`.gitlab-ci.yml`), so `composer install` runs on 8.3 and would fail if a dev tool required 8.4 or newer.

### W32: Pinstripe owns style and static analysis[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/build-and-supply-chain.html#w32-pinstripe-owns-style-and-static-analysis)

**Practice:** Use Pinstripe's Pint preset, PHPStan level 8 through Larastan, ESLint (flat config) and Prettier. No local overrides without a recorded reason.

**Stack:** `Checked`, for the PHP side. `composer.json` runs `pint --test`, `composer.json` runs `phpstan analyse`, and both are in the `ci` script (`composer.json`), which CI runs; `pint.json` uses the `laravel` preset and `phpstan.neon` sets `level: 8`. The JS side is configured but not yet in the CI pipeline: `eslint.config.js` (flat config) and `.prettierrc` exist, but no CI job runs `npm run lint` or `npm run format:check`. Pinstripe is not a dependency yet, so the presets are copied, not included.

### W33: Pin shared CI components to a commit[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/build-and-supply-chain.html#w33-pin-shared-ci-components-to-a-commit)

**Practice:** Preflight components are referenced by commit SHA or a fixed tag, not a moving branch.

**Stack:** `Documented`. `.gitlab-ci.yml` pins the `php-test` component to `@0.1.0` and `.github/workflows/ci.yml` pins the reusable workflow to a commit SHA; the comment "Pinned to Preflight 0.1.0. Never use ~latest." sits at `.gitlab-ci.yml`. There is no check that flags an unpinned include. Target `Checked`: PROCTOR flags `include:` entries without a SHA.

### Related[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/build-and-supply-chain.html#related)

- [Security](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/security.html)
- [Configuration](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/configuration.html)
- [Running WELD off Citadel](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/running-off-citadel.html)

## Check your setup[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/check-your-setup.html#check-your-setup)

Use `weld:doctor` to strike an arc across the local setup and see, one line per check, whether every joint holds.

### What it checks[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/check-your-setup.html#what-it-checks)

`weld:doctor` strikes an arc across the local setup and reports every joint: the app key, writable storage, the database and pending migrations. One line per check, PASS or WARN or FAIL. The checks, by name:

- `app-key`: PASS when `APP_KEY` is set; FAIL when it is empty, with a pointer to `php artisan key:generate`.
- `storage-writable`: PASS when `storage` and `bootstrap/cache` are both writable; FAIL when either is missing or not writable.
- `database`: PASS when the connection is up; FAIL names the exception class only, never the DSN, host or password.
- `migrations`: PASS when there are no pending migrations; WARN when some are pending (it lists them) or when it could not inspect them.

### Run it[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/check-your-setup.html#run-it)

Run it through the OS scripts or straight to the container:

```powershell
.\bin\weld.ps1 doctor
```

```sh
bin/weld.sh doctor
```

```sh
docker compose run --rm app php artisan weld:doctor
```

### Read the report[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/check-your-setup.html#read-the-report)

Each check prints one line: PASS, WARN or FAIL. The exit code is 1 when anything FAILs and 0 otherwise, so it works as a gate. Add `--json` to any of them for a machine-readable report. A good bead is a quiet one: all PASS and nothing to say.

Note

The standards checks (PHP version, debug in production, secure session cookies) belong to PROCTOR: run `composer proctor`, and the doctor report says so.

### Related[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/check-your-setup.html#related)

- [What is welded in](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/whats-welded-in.html)
- [Oracle](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/oracle.html)
- [Running WELD off Citadel](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/running-off-citadel.html)

---

Source: https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/container-contract.html

## The container contract[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/container-contract.html#the-container-contract)

This page lists the container contract practices for WELD, from the BEST_PRACTICES guide, with the tag that says whether the stack holds each one today.

### W9. Config comes from the environment only[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/container-contract.html#w9-config-comes-from-the-environment-only)

**Practice:** No `.env` in the image. Call `env()` only inside `config/*.php`.

**Why:** After `config:cache` the `.env` file is not loaded and `env()` returns `null` elsewhere.

**Stack:** `Documented`. Every `env()` call in the app is inside `config/*.php`; none is in `app/` or `routes/`. The one exception is `bootstrap/app.php`, which reads `TRUSTED_PROXIES` with `env()` because that closure runs before config loads (it carries a PHPStan ignore). Target `Checked`: Pinstripe/PROCTOR ban `env(` outside `config/`; the portability job boots without `.env`.

### W10. `config:cache` runs at container start, never at image build[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/container-contract.html#w10-config-cache-runs-at-container-start-never-at-image-build)

**Practice:** Build time may run `route:cache`, `view:cache`, `event:cache`. `php artisan optimize` at start is acceptable if the build did not freeze config.

**Why:** A build-time `config:cache` freezes the build machine's environment into the image.

**Stack:** `Documented`. The image build runs no artisan commands: `deploy/build.sh` fails if app source is present at build time, and the release step runs `php artisan optimize` once the environment is in place (`deploy/scripts/release.sh`, on by default, off with `SQUIRE_ARTISAN_OPTIMIZE=0`), so config is cached at deploy, never at build. Target `Checked`: PROCTOR scans the Dockerfile.

### W11. `/up` is the liveness endpoint, and it never checks the database[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/container-contract.html#w11-up-is-the-liveness-endpoint-and-it-never-checks-the-database)

**Practice:** Keep Laravel's `/up` (200 when the app boots). It must answer for any `Host`, over plain HTTP, before trusted hosts, redirects, sessions, CSP and auth. Put database and cache checks on a separate `/ready` endpoint, through the `DiagnosingHealth` event or a package.

**Why:** A database blip must not make the orchestrator kill every web container.

**Stack:** `Documented`. `bootstrap/app.php` sets the health route to `/up`, which answers 200 when the framework boots and touches no database. The `/ready` endpoint is not built yet. Target `Checked`: the portability job requests `/up` with `Host: 10.1.2.3:8080` and no forwarded headers, and again with the database stopped.

### W12. Image health check matches the platform[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/container-contract.html#w12-image-health-check-matches-the-platform)

**Practice:** Put a `HEALTHCHECK` in the Dockerfile that calls `/up` with a tool the image has (`curl` or `wget`). On Coolify a Dockerfile `HEALTHCHECK` takes precedence over the dashboard check, and a dashboard check needs `curl` or `wget` inside the container.

**Why:** Traefik will not route to an unhealthy container, and a missing tool makes a healthy app look dead.

**Stack:** `Documented`. The Dockerfile carries a `HEALTHCHECK` (`deploy/.squire/Dockerfile`) whose script asks the local web server for `/up` by default and reads no database (`deploy/health.php`, `deploy/health.php`). Target `Checked`: Preflight portability runs `docker inspect` for a health status of `healthy`.

### W13. Non-root, arbitrary UID in group 0, listen on 8080[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/container-contract.html#w13-non-root-arbitrary-uid-in-group-0-listen-on-8080)

**Practice:** Declare a non-root `USER`. Make writable paths group 0 and group-writable (`chgrp -R 0`, `chmod -R g=u`) for `storage/` and `bootstrap/cache/`. Do not depend on a `www-data` entry. Honor `PORT`.

**Why:** OpenShift runs a random UID in group 0 with all capabilities dropped.

**Stack:** `Not yet`. A Dockerfile now exists (`deploy/.squire/Dockerfile`), but it is the Citadel Apache image: it declares no `USER`, the vhost listens on 80 (`deploy/.squire/vhost.conf`) and the fallback base exposes 80 (`deploy/.squire/base-fallback.Dockerfile`), so the non-root, group-0, 8080 contract is not held. Target `Checked`: Preflight portability starts the image with a UID that has no `/etc/passwd` entry, `cap_drop: ALL`, `no-new-privileges` and a read-only root filesystem.

### W14. Logs go to stderr; the app writes only where it may[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/container-contract.html#w14-logs-go-to-stderr-the-app-writes-only-where-it-may)

**Practice:** Set `LOG_CHANNEL=stderr`. Nothing under `storage/logs`. Writes go to `storage/`, `bootstrap/cache/`, `/tmp` and declared volumes. Uploads go to object storage.

**Why:** Platforms collect stdout/stderr; local files vanish with the container.

**Stack:** `Documented`. `.env.example` sets `LOG_CHANNEL=stderr`. Target `Checked`: the portability job fails when `storage/logs` is non-empty.

### W15. Sessions and cache live in a shared store[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/container-contract.html#w15-sessions-and-cache-live-in-a-shared-store)

**Practice:** Use `SESSION_DRIVER=database` (or Redis) and a shared cache, even for one replica. Every host overlaps old and new containers during a deploy.

**Why:** A login must survive a hop between replicas.

**Stack:** `Documented`. `.env.example` sets `SESSION_DRIVER=database` and `.env.example` sets `CACHE_STORE=database`; `config/session.php` and `config/cache.php` default to the same. Target `Checked`: the portability job logs in on replica A and reads the session on replica B.

### W16. Stop cleanly on SIGTERM[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/container-contract.html#w16-stop-cleanly-on-sigterm)

**Practice:** Run PHP as PID 1 under a small init, or an entrypoint that `exec`s the server. Queue workers finish the current job on `SIGTERM`. Set the platform's grace period above the longest job `#[Timeout]`.

**Why:** A hard kill mid-job double-runs it after `retry_after`.

**Stack:** `Documented`. The entrypoint replaces the shell with the server (`deploy/.squire/fallback/citadel-apache-entrypoint`), so `SIGTERM` reaches the foreground process directly; no queue worker process type exists yet, and the grace period is a platform setting. Target `Checked`: the portability job sends `SIGTERM` and requires exit 0 within the grace period.

### W17. Trust proxies by preset, never `*` [#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/container-contract.html#w17-trust-proxies-by-preset-never)

**Practice:** Select a HELMET preset (`citadel` or `docker`), or list the front proxy in `HELMET_PROXIES` on other platforms. Do not paste `trustProxies(at: '*')` from tutorials. Set `APP_URL` and trusted hosts; Laravel trusts subdomains of `APP_URL` unless `subdomains: false`.

**Why:** An app that trusts all proxies lets a client forge `X-Forwarded-*` and the host used in callbacks.

**Stack:** `Enforced` by HELMET 0.3 (required `^0.3`): it trusts only the preset or listed proxies and drops `X-Forwarded-Port`. Target `Checked`: a portability probe sends forged `X-Forwarded-Host` and `-Proto` from an untrusted peer.

### How to read the tags[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/container-contract.html#how-to-read-the-tags)

Each practice ends with exactly one tag.

| Tag | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `Enforced` | WELD's code does it or refuses to run without it, and a test covers it. |
| `Checked` | PROCTOR or CI warns or fails. |
| `Documented` | Written down in the README or a config file, with no check behind it. |
| `Not yet` | A gap. |

### Related[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/container-contract.html#related)

- [App structure](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/app-structure.html)
- [Queues and scheduling](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/queues-and-scheduling.html)
- [Running WELD off Citadel](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/running-off-citadel.html)

Source: https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/oracle.html

## Oracle[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/oracle.html#oracle)

Set up and check WELD's Oracle connection: the settings, the plain-language check, and the parity image for a real connection from your machine.

### The wiring[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/oracle.html#the-wiring)

WELD speaks Oracle through `yajra/laravel-oci8`, and the wiring is already in: an `oracle` connection in `config/database.php`, a check command, and plain-language sentences for the common errors. Until you set the Oracle settings it stays dormant: nothing connects and nothing errors.

### Set the settings[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/oracle.html#set-the-settings)

Fill in one set of names in `.env` (the commented block in `.env.example`): `ORACLE_USERNAME`, `ORACLE_PASSWORD`, and either `ORACLE_TNS` (an Easy Connect string, `host:port/service`, or a full descriptor) or `ORACLE_HOST`, `ORACLE_PORT` and `ORACLE_SERVICE_NAME`. Leave them empty if your app does not use Oracle; nothing connects until they are set. On a server, set them in the app's environment settings, never in a file in git.

### Check the connection[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/oracle.html#check-the-connection)

Check the settings and the connection in plain language, one line per finding:

```
php artisan oracle:check
```

`oracle:check` is a thin wire to Squire's shared check file: it runs `deploy/oracle-check.php` with the current environment, streams the plain-language lines straight through, and returns the check's exit code, 0 when Oracle is not configured or all passed and 1 when a problem was found. The check file promises to never print a setting value. WELD does not own the check; a kit refresh (`vendor/bin/squire update`) puts the file here. If the check file is not there yet, the command tells you to run `vendor/bin/squire update` to get it.

### A real connection from your machine[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/oracle.html#a-real-connection-from-your-machine)

The local `app` container runs the stock Composer image, which has no Oracle driver. When you need a real connection from your machine, the Oracle-ready image is opt-in through `compose.oracle.yaml`:

```powershell
$env:WELD_ORACLE_IMAGE = "squire/oracle-parity:8.3"
docker compose -f compose.yaml -f compose.oracle.yaml up
```

```sh
WELD_ORACLE_IMAGE=squire/oracle-parity:8.3 docker compose -f compose.yaml -f compose.oracle.yaml up
```

The overlay swaps only the app's image and passes the `ORACLE_*` settings through from `.env`; the ports stay bound to `127.0.0.1`. It fails closed when `WELD_ORACLE_IMAGE` is unset.

`squire/oracle-parity:8.3` is the name Squire documents for its parity image; build it once with Squire's `scripts/oracle-image-build.sh --flavour parity --php 8.3` (the name is a placeholder until a registry is chosen).

### Related[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/oracle.html#related)

- [What is welded in](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/whats-welded-in.html)
- [Check your setup](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/check-your-setup.html)
- [Running WELD off Citadel](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/running-off-citadel.html)

Source: https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/queues-and-scheduling.html

## Queues and scheduling[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/queues-and-scheduling.html#queues-and-scheduling)

This page lists the queue and scheduling practices for WELD without Citadel workers, from the BEST_PRACTICES guide, with the tag that says whether the stack holds each one today.

### W18. Database queue by default; the worker is a process type[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/queues-and-scheduling.html#w18-database-queue-by-default-the-worker-is-a-process-type)

**Practice:** `QUEUE_CONNECTION=database`; run `php artisan queue:work --max-time=3600 --tries=3` as the `worker` process where the platform allows one. Use `#[Tries]`, `#[Timeout]` and `#[Backoff]` on jobs.

**Why:** It needs no extra service, and `--max-time` recycles memory.

**Stack:** `Documented`. `.env.example` sets `QUEUE_CONNECTION=database`, `config/queue.php` defaults to it, and the jobs tables are migrated by `database/migrations/0001_01_01_000002_create_jobs_table.php`. No job classes exist yet, so the `#[Tries]`/`#[Timeout]`/`#[Backoff]` attributes are not in use. Target `Checked`: a test that every job class declares `#[Tries]` and `#[Timeout]`.

### W19. Where no worker can run, run the queue from the scheduler[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/queues-and-scheduling.html#w19-where-no-worker-can-run-run-the-queue-from-the-scheduler)

**Practice:** On Citadel (no queue workers), schedule `queue:work --stop-when-empty --max-time=50 --tries=3` every minute with `withoutOverlapping` and a short expiry. Select it with `WELD_QUEUE_MODE=scheduled`.

**Why:** `--stop-when-empty` is documented for Docker use ("shutdown the container after the queue is empty"), and the scheduler is the one cron entry Citadel can run. This exact pattern is an inference, not a documented recipe.

**Stack:** `Not yet`. `routes/console.php` has no scheduler entries yet (only the `inspire` command). Target `Checked`: a test that `schedule:list` shows the entry under the `citadel` preset and not under the others.

### W20. Timeout below `retry_after` [#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/queues-and-scheduling.html#w20-timeout-below-retry-after)

**Practice:** Set each job timeout lower than the connection's `retry_after`. Timeouts need the PCNTL extension.

**Why:** Otherwise the job is attempted again before it has finished.

**Stack:** `Not yet`. No job classes exist yet. Target `Checked`: a config test comparing the two values; the image installs `pcntl`.

### W21. One scheduler entry; one run per task[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/queues-and-scheduling.html#w21-one-scheduler-entry-one-run-per-task)

**Practice:** Run `php artisan schedule:run` every minute (cron, or a CronJob), or `schedule:work` for a single long-lived container. With more than one scheduler, mark tasks `onOneServer()` (shared cache) and name closures.

**Why:** Three schedulers run a nightly report three times.

**Stack:** `Not yet`. `routes/console.php` has no scheduler entries yet. Target `Checked`: a test fails on any scheduled closure without `->name()`.

### W22. Interrupt and restart long-lived processes at deploy[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/queues-and-scheduling.html#w22-interrupt-and-restart-long-lived-processes-at-deploy)

**Practice:** After a release run `php artisan queue:restart` (or `php artisan reload`), and `schedule:interrupt` when sub-minute tasks exist.

**Why:** Workers and a minute-long `schedule:run` keep the old code until they exit.

**Stack:** `Not yet`. The release script now exists (`deploy/scripts/release.sh`) but runs none of `queue:restart`, `reload` or `schedule:interrupt`. Target `Checked`: the release script lists the three commands; PROCTOR checks the file.

### W23. Make a silent scheduler visible[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/queues-and-scheduling.html#w23-make-a-silent-scheduler-visible)

**Practice:** Record a heartbeat on every scheduler minute and fail `/ready` (not `/up`) when it is older than a few minutes. Export the age as a Prometheus gauge (off by default).

**Why:** With no worker supervisor, a stopped scheduler is otherwise invisible.

**Stack:** `Not yet`. There is no scheduler and no `/ready` endpoint yet. Target `Checked`: a test advances a fake clock and asserts `/ready` fails.

### W24. Run migrations exactly once per release[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/queues-and-scheduling.html#w24-run-migrations-exactly-once-per-release)

**Practice:** Use a Job, a pre-deploy hook (Coolify "Pre-deployment Command"), or `migrate --isolated`. Never run `migrate` in a per-replica entrypoint.

**Why:** Parallel replicas race on schema changes.

**Stack:** `Documented`. The release step runs `php artisan migrate --force` (`deploy/scripts/release.sh`) once per release, from the first-release hook (`deploy/deployments/001-first-release.sh`) and the Quick Update post-script (`deploy/scripts/release.sh`); the entrypoint itself runs no artisan commands (`deploy/.squire/fallback/citadel-apache-entrypoint`). Target `Checked`: PROCTOR flags `migrate` in an entrypoint.

### How to read the tags[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/queues-and-scheduling.html#how-to-read-the-tags)

Each practice ends with exactly one tag.

| Tag | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `Enforced` | WELD's code does it or refuses to run without it, and a test covers it. |
| `Checked` | PROCTOR or CI warns or fails. |
| `Documented` | Written down in the README or a config file, with no check behind it. |
| `Not yet` | A gap. |

### Related[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/queues-and-scheduling.html#related)

- [App structure](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/app-structure.html)
- [The container contract](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/container-contract.html)
- [Running WELD off Citadel](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/running-off-citadel.html)
