## Quick start[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/quick-start.html#quick-start)

This page takes a fresh copy of WELD from a folder to a running, checked app on your machine.

One command strikes the spark; the containers do the welding. Docker is the only prerequisite: PHP and Node run in the containers, so the host needs neither.

### Steps[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/quick-start.html#steps)

1. Bring the stack up:
   ```powershell
   .\bin\weld.ps1 up
   ```
   ```sh
   bin/weld.sh up
   ```
   Expected: `up` copies `.env.example` to `.env` if it is missing, installs the PHP and Node dependencies in the containers, starts the app and Vite, generates the app key if it is not set, and runs the migrations.
2. Open [http://localhost:8000](http://localhost:8000). Expected: the app, served by the local stack.
3. Run the doctor:
   ```powershell
   .\bin\weld.ps1 doctor
   ```
   ```sh
   bin/weld.sh doctor
   ```
   Expected: one line per check, PASS or WARN or FAIL; exit code 1 when anything FAILs. A good bead is a quiet one: all PASS and nothing to say.
4. Run the checks:
   ```powershell
   .\bin\weld.ps1 test
   ```
   ```sh
   bin/weld.sh test
   ```
   Expected: `composer ci` runs in the app container: validate, tests, Pint, PHPStan level 8, the agent-ready check and audit.

### The subcommands[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/quick-start.html#the-subcommands)

The same subcommands work on every OS:

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `up` | Bring the whole stack up, as above |
| `down` | Stop and remove the containers |
| `test` | Run `composer ci` in the app container |
| `doctor` | Run `php artisan weld:doctor` in the app container |
| `logs` | Follow the container logs |

### What you built[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/quick-start.html#what-you-built)

You have WELD running locally in Docker: the app and Vite in containers, `.env` copied from `.env.example`, the app key generated and the migrations run. That is the whole Wayne State app stack joined into one application, with sign-in, security headers, checks, coding standards, CI and the WayneUI interface already hooked up.

### Next steps[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/quick-start.html#next-steps)

- Make it yours: rename the four things that still say WELD (the composer name, the app name, the site title and the git remote), give the copy its own key, and re-run the checks.
- [Check your setup](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/check-your-setup.html): what the doctor reports, joint by joint.
- [What is welded in](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/whats-welded-in.html): the parts and what each does in the app.
- [Running WELD off Citadel](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/running-off-citadel.html): for when the destination is somewhere other than a laptop.

- [Overview](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/index.html)
- [Install](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/install.html)

## Is WELD still Sourdough's shape?[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/regen-check.html#is-weld-still-sourdough-s-shape)

This page shows how the regen gate proves that WELD is still Sourdough's Inertia shape, and how to run it against your own generation.

### How the check works[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/regen-check.html#how-the-check-works)

Sourdough writes a manifest of every file it generates (`.sourdough/manifest.json`: each path with its SHA-256). `bin/regen-check.php` compares that manifest with WELD file by file, skipping the product files WELD adds on top (listed in `.sourdough/product-files.json`) and any path with a `vendor` or `node_modules` segment. Each remaining path is reported as IDENTICAL, DIFFERS or MISSING_IN_WELD.

The generated app folder must contain `.sourdough/manifest.json`, the file list Sourdough writes into every app it generates (files maps path to `{class, sha256}`). Paths listed in `.sourdough/product-files.json` (exact paths or `dir/` prefixes) and every path with a `vendor` or `node_modules` segment at any depth are skipped. A DIFFERS path means the WELD file exists with another SHA-256.

### The ratchet baseline[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/regen-check.html#the-ratchet-baseline)

The gate is a ratchet: `.sourdough/regen-baseline.json` records the drift already known and accepted, and the check fails only on new drift. CI runs it against a fresh `sourdough new --inertia` generation from Sourdough's main; locally, point it at your own generation.

### Running the check[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/regen-check.html#running-the-check)

Run the check:

```sh
php bin/regen-check.php --generated <dir>
```

or through Composer:

```sh
composer regen-check -- --generated <dir>
```

Record the current drift as accepted: add `--write-baseline`.

Note

Exit codes: 0 no new drift (or the baseline was written), 1 new drift, listed on stderr, 2 usage error. The script is plain PHP 8.3 with no Composer packages, so it runs on Windows, macOS and Linux the same way.

### Related[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/regen-check.html#related)

- [WELD and Sourdough](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/sourdough.html)
- [Status](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/status.html)
- [Changelog](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/changelog.html)

Source: https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/security.html

## Security[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/security.html#security)

This page states WELD's security practices, one per heading, each with the rule and the tag that shows whether the stack holds it today.

### W25: Keep the framework above the published security floor[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/security.html#w25-keep-the-framework-above-the-published-security-floor)

**Practice:** Require `laravel/framework` at or above the latest patched release, run `composer audit` in CI, and let CREED's `policy.json` name the minimum patch level. A critical TokenGuard authentication bypass was published on 2026-10-19 (fixed in 13.29.0 and 12.68.0).

**Stack:** `Checked`. `composer.json` pins `laravel/framework: ^13.29` (at or above the patched release), `composer.json` runs `@composer audit` inside the `ci` script, and `.gitlab-ci.yml` includes the Preflight `composer-audit` component, so the audit runs in CI. CREED's `policy.json` is a dependency and PROCTOR measures against it, now also inside the test suite (`tests/Feature/ProctorCheckTest.php`).

### W26: Debug is off outside local[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/security.html#w26-debug-is-off-outside-local)

Warning

`APP_DEBUG=false` in production. Debug pages expose configuration values, and the debug page has had an XSS advisory (Low, 2026-09-10).

**Practice:** `APP_DEBUG=false` in production. The debug page has had an XSS advisory (Low, 2026-09-10).

**Stack:** `Not yet`. `.env.example` sets `APP_DEBUG=true` for the local default, and there is no boot assertion that fails when `APP_ENV=production` and `APP_DEBUG=true`. Target `Enforced`: a boot assertion fails when `APP_ENV=production` and `APP_DEBUG=true`.

### W27: CSRF uses the PreventRequestForgery middleware[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/security.html#w27-csrf-uses-the-preventrequestforgery-middleware)

**Practice:** Laravel 13 formalized request-forgery protection as `PreventRequestForgery` (origin-aware, still token-compatible). Any custom middleware stack or HELMET code must reference the new name.

**Stack:** `Documented`. `bootstrap/app.php` appends to the default `web` middleware group, which carries `PreventRequestForgery` in Laravel 13, so the protection is in place by default. There is no feature test that posts without a token and expects 419. Target `Checked`: a feature test posts without a token and expects 419.

### W28: CSP works with Inertia 3 and Vite[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/security.html#w28-csp-works-with-inertia-3-and-vite)

**Practice:** HELMET sets the CSP header and calls `Vite::useCspNonce()`; Laravel then adds the nonce to the tags `@vite` emits. Inertia 3 puts initial page data in a JSON script element. Run the policy in report-only first.

**Stack:** `Documented`. HELMET `^0.3` is a dependency and its security headers and CSP middleware run in the global chain. Target `Checked`: a browser test under an enforced CSP.

### W29: Agent tooling stays out of production[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/security.html#w29-agent-tooling-stays-out-of-production)

Warning

A dev tool with write and query abilities is attack surface. Its MCP server can write rules to disk and run database queries, and its docs tool sends queries to a hosted service. Keep it out of production: build production images with `composer install --no-dev`.

**Practice:** Laravel Boost is `require-dev`. Its MCP server can write rules to disk and run database queries; its docs tool sends queries to a hosted service. Production images are built with `composer install --no-dev`; guard any `post-update-cmd` that calls `boost:update`.

**Stack:** `Not yet`. Boost is not a dependency yet. Target `Checked`: the portability job fails when `vendor/laravel/boost` exists in the image.

### Related[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/security.html#related)

- [Build and supply chain](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/build-and-supply-chain.html)
- [Configuration](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/configuration.html)
- [Running WELD off Citadel](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/running-off-citadel.html)

## WELD and Sourdough[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/sourdough.html#weld-and-sourdough)

This page explains how Sourdough and WELD divide the work of starting a Wayne State app, and which one to pick for your project.

### What Sourdough does[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/sourdough.html#what-sourdough-does)

Sourdough is the starter tool for every shape of Wayne State app. It bakes four shapes today: raw PHP, Laravel with Blade, Laravel with Blade plus Vue islands, and Laravel with Inertia and Vue; only raw PHP with a Vue SPA is not available yet.

### Where WELD sits[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/sourdough.html#where-weld-sits)

WELD is one of those shapes, Laravel with Inertia and Vue, with every part already joined and proved to work together. In other words, WELD is the Laravel + Inertia/Vue shape that Sourdough's templates describe, already shaped.

Note

Pick Sourdough when you want a starter you shape yourself. Pick WELD when you want the finished piece.

### Where changes belong[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/sourdough.html#where-changes-belong)

If every app should get a change, it belongs in Sourdough; if only this shape should, it lives here.

### Related[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/sourdough.html#related)

- [Is WELD still Sourdough's shape?](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/regen-check.html)

- [Quick start](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/quick-start.html)

## What is welded in[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/whats-welded-in.html#what-is-welded-in)

This page lists the parts welded into WELD, what each one does in the app, and what is on the bench today.

### The parts[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/whats-welded-in.html#the-parts)

| Part | What it does in WELD |
| --- | --- |
| WayneUI | The interface: Wayne State's design system, wired into the Vue front end and Blade layouts |
| CREED | The written standards and `policy.json`: supported PHP, Laravel and Node versions |
| Pinstripe | The coding standard: Pint, PHPStan level 8, ESLint and Prettier |
| Preflight | The CI pipeline, from GitLab CI/CD components |
| PROCTOR | The checks, run in CI and as the deploy gate |
| SESAME | Sign-in: CAS, Entra ID (OpenID Connect) and the auth gateway driver, and app-native sessions |
| HELMET | The baseline runtime: security headers and CSP, sessions, trusted proxies, `/up` |
| Ziggy | Route names as URLs: the route list ships inside the Vite bundle, so `route()` works in Vue without an inline script |

![WELD's journey, one request and six stops joined by a gold seam: HELMET sets security headers, SESAME signs the user in, WayneUI renders the page, PROCTOR checks the code, Preflight runs CI, Squire deploys.](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/readme/journey.svg)

One request, six stops, one seam. The bead runs the length of it; with reduced motion on, it stays put.

### What is on the bench today[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/whats-welded-in.html#what-is-on-the-bench-today)

HELMET, SESAME and PROCTOR are welded in from Packagist; the rest of the cast is on Packagist too and gets welded on in turn.

- `composer.json` is `waynestate/weld`, requires PHP `^8.3`, and the lock file resolves for 8.3.0
- `.env.example` sets `APP_NAME=WELD`, `LOG_CHANNEL=stderr` and `SESSION_DRIVER=database`
- `Schema::defaultStringLength(191)` keeps index keys under Citadel's MySQL 5.6 767-byte cap
- `.gitattributes` sets `* text=auto eol=lf`
- `composer ci` is the CI contract: it runs validate, tests, Pint, PHPStan level 8, the agent-ready check and audit, the same command on GitLab and GitHub
- `pint.json` and `phpstan.neon` still copy Pinstripe's 0.1 Laravel presets; Pinstripe 0.1.1 is on Packagist (tagged), and they switch to `includes: vendor/waynestate/pinstripe/...` when WELD requires it
- HELMET runs its security headers and CSP middleware in the global chain, so every response carries the baseline; the Vite build takes the per-request nonce; trusted proxies are a literal list in `bootstrap/app.php`; `/up` stays Laravel's built-in health route
- SESAME owns sign-in at `/login` and `/logout`; the fake driver stands in for the identity provider locally, and CAS is an env change away
- PROCTOR measures WELD against CREED's `policy.json` as a CI job (`composer proctor`): warnings pass, failures block
- The starter kit's password auth (register, login, password reset, two-factor) is removed on purpose; the door is SESAME's
- The license is MIT

### Related[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/whats-welded-in.html#related)

- [Check your setup](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/check-your-setup.html)
- [Oracle](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/oracle.html)
- [Running WELD off Citadel](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/running-off-citadel.html)

## Overview[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/#overview)

This page orients you to WELD: what it is, which path to pick first, and where the project stands today.

[![WELD's front page: the headline WELD, 'Wired, Everything, Linked, Deployed. Many parts, one piece.', the composer create-project command, and the welder's-helmet mark on a green tile.](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/readme/hero.jpg)](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/index.html)

**WELD**

![php ^8.3](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/readme/badges/php.svg) ![laravel ^13.29](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/readme/badges/laravel.svg) ![license MIT](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/readme/badges/license.svg)

**W**ired, **E**verything, **L**inked, **D**eployed. Many parts, one piece.

WELD is the whole Wayne State app stack joined into one application. Install it, deploy it, and every part is already hooked up: sign-in, security headers, checks, coding standards, CI and the WayneUI interface. Think of it as the Megazord, except it comes with a deploy script and nobody has to shout to make it combine. Fourteen parts, one bead.

### Pick your path[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/#pick-your-path)

- [Quick start](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/quick-start.html): bring the whole stack up with one Docker command.
- [Install](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/install.html): get a copy with composer create-project, or clone it if you want the history too.
- [What is welded in](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/whats-welded-in.html): the parts and what each does in the app.
- [Running WELD off Citadel](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/running-off-citadel.html): OpenShift, Coolify and plain Docker, with Citadel for comparison.

### Status[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/#status)

Latest release: 0.1.2 (2026-11-03). The license is MIT.

**Not to be confused with:** `weld:doctor` checks local setup only; standards checks are PROCTOR's.

Agents: fetch [https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/llms.txt](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/llms.txt).

## Install[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/install.html#install)

This page gets you a working copy of WELD: what it needs, the two ways to get it, and how to verify the result.

### Requirements[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/install.html#requirements)

- PHP `^8.3`
- Laravel `^13.29`
- Node, for `npm ci`
- Docker, for the local stack

Note

To run WELD locally, Docker is the only prerequisite: PHP and Node run in the containers, so the host needs neither.

### Get it[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/install.html#get-it)

WELD is an app you start from, not a library you require. The Megazord ships in a repo, not a box. Composer makes you a fresh copy, writes `.env`, generates the app key and runs the first migration:

```sh
composer create-project waynestate/weld my-app
cd my-app
npm ci
```

Or clone it, if you want the history too, and it is yours to rename:

```sh
git clone https://github.com/waynestate/weld.git my-app
cd my-app
composer install
php vendor/bin/advisor install --client=claude --write
npm ci
# Windows (PowerShell):
Copy-Item .env.example .env
# Linux/macOS:
cp .env.example .env
php artisan key:generate
```

Note

The `advisor install` line writes `.mcp.json`, the MCP config that points Claude Code at ADVISOR's server; the file is git-ignored, because a committed `.mcp.json` would run a program on whoever opens the project. Set `ADVISOR_ENABLED=1` in `.env` to switch the advisor on.

### Verify[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/install.html#verify)

Run the checks the way CI does. `composer ci` is the CI contract: it runs validate, tests, Pint, PHPStan level 8, the agent-ready check and audit, the same command on GitLab and GitHub. The `test` subcommand runs it in the app container: `.\bin\weld.ps1 test` on Windows (PowerShell), `bin/weld.sh test` on macOS / Linux.

The doctor strikes an arc across the local setup: `.\bin\weld.ps1 doctor` on Windows (PowerShell), `bin/weld.sh doctor` on macOS / Linux. It reports one line per check, PASS or WARN or FAIL, and exits with code 1 when anything FAILs, so it works as a gate. A good bead is a quiet one: all PASS and nothing to say.

### Next steps[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/install.html#next-steps)

- [Quick start](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/quick-start.html): bring the stack up with one command and open the app.
- [What is welded in](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/whats-welded-in.html): the parts already hooked up in your copy.
- [Check your setup](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/check-your-setup.html): what the doctor reports, joint by joint.

### Related[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/install.html#related)

- [Overview](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/index.html)
- [Quick start](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/quick-start.html)
- [What is welded in](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/whats-welded-in.html)
- [Check your setup](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/check-your-setup.html)

## Commands[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/commands.html#commands)

This page is the reference for every command a WELD app runs: the `bin/weld` subcommands, the composer scripts, and the artisan and bin PHP commands, with what each one does.

### The bin/weld subcommands[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/commands.html#the-bin-weld-subcommands)

One command strikes the spark; the containers do the welding. Docker is the only prerequisite: PHP and Node run in the containers, so the host needs neither. The same subcommands work on every OS.

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `up` | Copy `.env.example` to `.env` if missing, install the PHP and Node dependencies in the containers, write `.mcp.json` from ADVISOR, start the app and Vite, generate the app key if needed, and migrate |
| `down` | Stop and remove the containers |
| `test` | Run `composer ci` in the app container |
| `doctor` | Run `php artisan weld:doctor` in the app container |
| `logs` | Follow the container logs; Ctrl+C stops |

Tip

`up` finishes with a pointer to open [http://localhost:8000](http://localhost:8000). Skip the ADVISOR step with `--no-advisor` (`-NoAdvisor` on Windows).

Bring the whole stack up:

```powershell
.\bin\weld.ps1 up
```

```sh
bin/weld.sh up
```

Run the full check suite in the app container:

```powershell
.\bin\weld.ps1 test
```

```sh
bin/weld.sh test
```

Check your setup:

```powershell
.\bin\weld.ps1 doctor
```

```sh
bin/weld.sh doctor
```

Follow the container logs:

```powershell
.\bin\weld.ps1 logs
```

```sh
bin/weld.sh logs
```

Stop and remove the containers:

```powershell
.\bin\weld.ps1 down
```

```sh
bin/weld.sh down
```

### Composer scripts[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/commands.html#composer-scripts)

| Script | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `composer test` | Pest, running the PHPUnit class tests and the Pest tests side by side |
| `composer lint` | Run Pint as a check (`pint --test`) |
| `composer fix` | Apply Pint fixes (`pint`) |
| `composer analyse` | Run PHPStan analysis (`phpstan analyse --memory-limit=1G`) |
| `composer proctor` | PROCTOR against CREED's policy |
| `composer ziggy` | Confirm the Ziggy routes are current: `composer ziggy`, then `git diff --exit-code resources/js/ziggy.*` |
| `composer regen-check` | Compare a freshly generated Sourdough Inertia app with WELD by SHA-256 and fail only on new drift versus `.sourdough/regen-baseline.json`; pass `--generated <dir>` (and optionally `--write-baseline`) through |
| `composer ci` | Runs `composer validate --strict`, the tests, Pint, PHPStan, the agent-ready and docs checks and `composer audit`; it does not run PROCTOR, Ziggy or the JS lint |
| `composer site:agent-ready` | Rewrite the Markdown twins, llms.txt, llms-full.txt, robots.txt and sitemap.xml in site/ (Squire's agent-ready kit) |
| `composer site:agent-ready-check` | Fail when the agent-ready files are stale, a page lacks its Markdown link, a prompt drifts from the docs, or the kit was edited here |
| `composer docs` | Write site/docs/ from docs/ with the shared docs builder, and generate docs/changelog.md from CHANGELOG.md |
| `composer docs:check` | Fail when the committed docs site is stale or the docs carry findings; writes nothing |

### Artisan and bin PHP commands[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/commands.html#artisan-and-bin-php-commands)

#### `php artisan weld:doctor` [#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/commands.html#php-artisan-weld-doctor)

`weld:doctor` strikes an arc across the local setup and reports every joint: the app key, writable storage, the database and pending migrations. One line per check, PASS or WARN or FAIL; exit code 1 when anything FAILs, so it works as a gate. The standards checks (PHP version, debug in production, secure session cookies) belong to PROCTOR: run `composer proctor`, and the doctor report says so. A good bead is a quiet one: all PASS and nothing to say.

Add `--json` to any of these for a machine-readable report. Run it through the `doctor` subcommand above, or straight to the container:

```powershell
.\bin\weld.ps1 doctor
```

```sh
bin/weld.sh doctor
```

```sh
docker compose run --rm app php artisan weld:doctor
```

#### `php bin/regen-check.php` [#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/commands.html#php-bin-regen-check-php)

`bin/regen-check.php` compares a freshly generated Sourdough Inertia app (its `.sourdough/manifest.json`, each path with its SHA-256) with WELD file by file, skipping the product files listed in `.sourdough/product-files.json` and any `vendor` or `node_modules` path. Each remaining path is reported as IDENTICAL, DIFFERS, MISSING_IN_WELD or RELOCATED. The gate is a ratchet: `.sourdough/regen-baseline.json` records the drift already known and accepted, and the check fails only on new drift. It is not part of `composer ci`; CI runs it as a separate, warning-only job.

- Run the check: `php bin/regen-check.php --generated <dir>` (or `composer regen-check -- --generated <dir>`)
- Record the current drift as accepted: add `--write-baseline`

#### `php bin/agent-ready.php` [#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/commands.html#php-bin-agent-ready-php)

- `php bin/agent-ready.php`: rewrite the Markdown twins, llms.txt, llms-full.txt, robots.txt and sitemap.xml in site/ (Squire's agent-ready kit).
- `php bin/agent-ready.php --check`: fail when the agent-ready files are stale, a page lacks its Markdown link, a prompt drifts from the docs, or the kit was edited here.

These run as `composer site:agent-ready` and `composer site:agent-ready-check`.

#### `php bin/docs-site.php` [#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/commands.html#php-bin-docs-site-php)

- `php bin/docs-site.php`: write site/docs/ from docs/ with the shared docs builder, and generate docs/changelog.md from CHANGELOG.md.
- `php bin/docs-site.php --check`: fail when the committed docs site is stale or the docs carry findings; writes nothing.

These run as `composer docs` and `composer docs:check`. The docs are built from `docs/` by the shared docs builder and checked in `composer ci`, so the page you read is the page that ships.

- [Is WELD still Sourdough's shape?](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/regen-check.html)

## Configuration[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/configuration.html#configuration)

This page lists every environment variable a WELD app reads, its default from `.env.example`, and what the sources say about it.

### Environment variables[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/configuration.html#environment-variables)

| Name | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `APP_NAME` | `WELD` | Renamed when you clone and rename; `VITE_APP_NAME` follows it through `${APP_NAME}`. |
| `APP_ENV` | `local` |  |
| `APP_KEY` | `(empty)` | Generate it with `php artisan key:generate`; `weld:doctor` checks the app key. |
| `APP_DEBUG` | `true` | The local default; keep `APP_DEBUG=false` in production (W26). |
| `APP_URL` | `http://localhost` | Set it to the real host (W17); Laravel trusts subdomains of `APP_URL` unless `subdomains: false`. |
| `APP_LOCALE` | `en` |  |
| `APP_FALLBACK_LOCALE` | `en` |  |
| `APP_FAKER_LOCALE` | `en_US` |  |
| `APP_MAINTENANCE_DRIVER` | `file` |  |
| `APP_MAINTENANCE_STORE` | `database (commented out)` |  |
| `PHP_CLI_SERVER_WORKERS` | `4` |  |
| `BCRYPT_ROUNDS` | `12` |  |
| `LOG_CHANNEL` | `stderr` | Everything goes to `php://stderr`; nothing under `storage/logs` (W14). |
| `LOG_STACK` | `single` |  |
| `LOG_DEPRECATIONS_CHANNEL` | `null` |  |
| `LOG_LEVEL` | `debug` |  |
| `DB_CONNECTION` | `sqlite` | Local development uses SQLite. |
| `DB_HOST` | `127.0.0.1 (commented out)` |  |
| `DB_PORT` | `3306 (commented out)` |  |
| `DB_DATABASE` | `laravel (commented out)` |  |
| `DB_USERNAME` | `root (commented out)` |  |
| `DB_PASSWORD` | `(empty, commented out)` |  |
| `ORACLE_USERNAME` | `(empty, commented out)` | Leave empty if the app does not use Oracle; nothing connects until set. On a server, set it in the app's environment settings, never in a file in git. |
| `ORACLE_PASSWORD` | `(empty, commented out)` | As `ORACLE_USERNAME`; on a server, set it in the app's environment settings, never in a file in git. |
| `ORACLE_TNS` | `(empty, commented out)` | An Easy Connect string (`host:port/service`) or a full descriptor; set this or the host, port and service trio. |
| `ORACLE_HOST` | `(empty, commented out)` | Set with `ORACLE_PORT` and `ORACLE_SERVICE_NAME` as the alternative to `ORACLE_TNS`. |
| `ORACLE_PORT` | `(empty, commented out)` | Part of the host, port and service alternative to `ORACLE_TNS`. |
| `ORACLE_SERVICE_NAME` | `(empty, commented out)` | Part of the host, port and service alternative to `ORACLE_TNS`. |
| `SESSION_DRIVER` | `database` | A shared store, even for one replica (W15). |
| `SESSION_LIFETIME` | `120` |  |
| `SESSION_ENCRYPT` | `false` |  |
| `SESSION_PATH` | `/` |  |
| `SESSION_DOMAIN` | `null` |  |
| `TRUSTED_PROXIES` | `172.18.0.1` | Which proxies Laravel trusts for `X-Forwarded-Proto` and the client address. Unset keeps `172.18.0.1` (Citadel's proxy); set but empty trusts none; `*` trusts every proxy; or a comma-separated list of IPs and CIDR ranges. Off Citadel, set your own proxy here and put the same list in `HELMET_PROXIES`. |
| `HELMET_PROXIES` | `172.18.0.1` | The address HA-Proxy connects from; the same list as `trustProxies` in `bootstrap/app.php`. Empty trusts nothing. A platform preset fills the list instead; when both are set, `HELMET_PROXIES` wins, and an unknown preset name throws at boot. |
| `HELMET_PRESET` | `citadel (commented out)` | Picks a platform preset; HELMET ships two, `citadel` and `docker`. An unknown preset name throws at boot. When both it and `HELMET_PROXIES` are set, `HELMET_PROXIES` wins. |
| `SESAME_DRIVER` | `fake` | SESAME owns sign-in. `fake` signs in locally without an identity provider and refuses to boot outside development environments; production sets `SESAME_DRIVER=cas` plus `SESAME_CAS_BASE_URL`. |
| `SESAME_FAKE_USERNAME` | `jdoe` |  |
| `SESAME_CAS_BASE_URL` | `(empty, commented out)` | Set with `SESAME_DRIVER=cas` in production. |
| `SESAME_CAS_SERVICE_URL` | `(empty, commented out)` |  |
| `BROADCAST_CONNECTION` | `log` |  |
| `FILESYSTEM_DISK` | `local` |  |
| `QUEUE_CONNECTION` | `database` | Run the queue worker where the platform allows one (W18). |
| `CACHE_STORE` | `database` | A shared cache, even for one replica (W15). |
| `CACHE_PREFIX` | `(empty, commented out)` |  |
| `MEMCACHED_HOST` | `127.0.0.1` |  |
| `REDIS_CLIENT` | `phpredis` |  |
| `REDIS_HOST` | `127.0.0.1` |  |
| `REDIS_PASSWORD` | `null` |  |
| `REDIS_PORT` | `6379` |  |
| `MAIL_MAILER` | `log` |  |
| `MAIL_SCHEME` | `null` |  |
| `MAIL_HOST` | `127.0.0.1` |  |
| `MAIL_PORT` | `2525` |  |
| `MAIL_USERNAME` | `null` |  |
| `MAIL_PASSWORD` | `null` |  |
| `MAIL_FROM_ADDRESS` | `hello@example.com` |  |
| `MAIL_FROM_NAME` | `${APP_NAME}` |  |
| `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID` | `(empty)` |  |
| `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY` | `(empty)` |  |
| `AWS_DEFAULT_REGION` | `us-east-1` |  |
| `AWS_BUCKET` | `(empty)` |  |
| `AWS_USE_PATH_STYLE_ENDPOINT` | `false` |  |
| `VITE_APP_NAME` | `${APP_NAME}` | Follows `APP_NAME` through `${APP_NAME}`. |

### Trusted proxies and HELMET_PRESET[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/configuration.html#trusted-proxies-and-helmet-preset)

HELMET owns the trusted proxies (W17, `Enforced` by HELMET 0.2): it trusts only the preset or listed proxies and drops `X-Forwarded-Port`. Pick a platform preset with `HELMET_PRESET`; HELMET 0.2 ships two, `citadel` and `docker`, and an unknown preset name throws at boot. On other platforms, list the front proxy's address in `HELMET_PROXIES` (it wins over `HELMET_PRESET`), and never trust a whole private range. Do not paste `trustProxies(at: '*')` from tutorials: an app that trusts all proxies lets a client forge `X-Forwarded-*` and the host used in callbacks. Laravel's own proxy list has its own variable; set `TRUSTED_PROXIES` to the same address (unset means Citadel's `172.18.0.1`). In WELD today, trusted proxies are a literal list in `bootstrap/app.php`.

### Keep .env out of version control[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/configuration.html#keep-env-out-of-version-control)

Warning

`.env` never goes into version control. On a server, set values in the app's environment settings, never in a file in git.

## Status[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/status.html#status)

This page records what is on the bench today: the state of every part welded into WELD, plus the gaps still open for the backlog.

HELMET, SESAME and PROCTOR are welded in from Packagist; the rest of the cast is on Packagist too and gets welded on in turn. For what each part does in WELD, see [What is welded in](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/whats-welded-in.html).

### What is on the bench today[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/status.html#what-is-on-the-bench-today)

| Item | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `composer.json` | `waynestate/weld`, requires PHP `^8.3`, and the lock file resolves for 8.3.0 |
| `.env.example` | sets `APP_NAME=WELD`, `LOG_CHANNEL=stderr` and `SESSION_DRIVER=database` |
| Index length | `Schema::defaultStringLength(191)` keeps index keys under Citadel's MySQL 5.6 767-byte cap |
| `.gitattributes` | sets `* text=auto eol=lf` |
| CI contract | `composer ci` runs validate, tests, Pint, PHPStan level 8, the agent-ready check and audit, the same command on GitLab and GitHub |
| Pinstripe presets | `pint.json` and `phpstan.neon` still copy Pinstripe's 0.1 Laravel presets; Pinstripe 0.1.1 is on Packagist (tagged), and they switch to `includes: vendor/waynestate/pinstripe/...` when WELD requires it |
| HELMET | runs its security headers and CSP middleware in the global chain, so every response carries the baseline; the Vite build takes the per-request nonce; trusted proxies are a literal list in `bootstrap/app.php`; `/up` stays Laravel's built-in health route |
| SESAME | owns sign-in at `/login` and `/logout`; the fake driver stands in for the identity provider locally, and CAS is an env change away |
| PROCTOR | measures WELD against CREED's `policy.json` as a CI job (`composer proctor`): warnings pass, failures block |
| Password auth | the starter kit's password auth (register, login, password reset, two-factor) is removed on purpose; the door is SESAME's |
| License | MIT |

### Gaps for the backlog[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/status.html#gaps-for-the-backlog)

The Laravel base has landed; the gaps below are the stack packages and the deploy path that have not.

- The stack packages are dependencies now: SESAME and HELMET in `require`, CREED and PROCTOR in `require-dev`, all from Packagist. The items that waited on them (SESAME W1, HELMET W17 and W28, PROCTOR's `Checked` targets, CREED W25) can be checked against the installed packages. Preflight portability (W8, W10, W12, W13, W16, W24), Pinstripe (W2, W32) and WayneUI (W2) are not wired into WELD yet.
- The Squire kit in `deploy/` now carries the Citadel deploy path: a Dockerfile mirroring the platform image, an entrypoint and an idempotent release script, so W10, W12, W16 and W24 hold for that path. Still plans: worker and scheduler process types (W8), the non-root, group-0, 8080 contract (W13), the restart commands in the release script (W22), and the deploy-time queue/scheduler work (W19, W21, W23).
- The JS side of the coding standard (W32) is configured but not in CI.
- Unverified: OpenShift arbitrary-UID text on a primary Red Hat page; `serversideup/php` behavior under a random UID; Pest 4's PHP floor; `spatie/laravel-health` scheduler and queue checks; whether Laravel's health route runs before `TrustHosts`; whether the old CSRF middleware name is still an alias.
- Decision needed: queue mode on Citadel (W19). The scheduled-worker pattern is a stopgap. Confirm with the deploy kit project whether Citadel can run a cron-driven `schedule:run` at all.
- Decision needed: `spatie/laravel-health` or our own `/ready` (W11, W23).
- Decision needed: whether WELD keeps Fortify for a non-SSO mode.
- Decision needed: SSR on by default or off.

## Running WELD off Citadel[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/running-off-citadel.html#running-weld-off-citadel)

WELD deploys on Citadel through Squire: one container per app, and builds run at release time inside the app container. The stack rule (ADR-0010, portable beyond Citadel) says the same app must also run on OpenShift, Coolify and plain Docker. This page is the per-platform contract: how traffic reaches the app, where logs go, what may be written, which user runs it, how the platform knows it is alive, and what to run after every deploy.

Two notes before the tables. Claims marked **(check)** depend on something not built yet:

- There is no production Dockerfile or entrypoint. `compose.yaml` is the local development stack (`artisan serve` on 8000 plus Vite on 5173, SQLite), not a deploy image.
- HELMET (`^0.2`) owns the trusted proxies (BEST_PRACTICES.md, W17). `HELMET_PRESET` picks a platform preset, and HELMET 0.2 ships two: `citadel` and `docker`. An unknown preset name throws at boot. Anywhere else, list the front proxy's address in `HELMET_PROXIES` (it wins over `HELMET_PRESET`), and never trust a whole private range. Laravel's own proxy list has its own variable: set TRUSTED_PROXIES to the same address (unset means Citadel's 172.18.0.1).

### Common ground, every platform[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/running-off-citadel.html#common-ground-every-platform)

| Concern | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| Config | Environment only. No `.env` in the image; `env()` calls live in `config/` (W9). Set `APP_URL` to the real host (W17) and keep `APP_DEBUG=false` in production (W26). |
| Logs | `LOG_CHANNEL=stderr` (`.env.example:18`). Everything goes to `php://stderr`; nothing under `storage/logs` (W14). |
| Writable paths | `storage/` and `bootstrap/cache/` only, plus `/tmp` (W14). |
| Sessions and cache | A shared store, even for one replica: `SESSION_DRIVER=database` (`.env.example:30`) and `CACHE_STORE=database` (`.env.example:40`), because every deploy overlaps old and new containers (W15). |
| User | Non-root. Declare a `USER` in the image; never depend on a `www-data` entry (W13). |
| Health | `/up`, registered in `bootstrap/app.php`: 200 when the framework boots, and it never checks the database, so a database blip cannot kill every replica (W11). |
| After every deploy | Run `php artisan weld:doctor` in the app container. One PASS, WARN or FAIL line per check; exit code 1 when anything FAILs, so it works as a gate. |

### Citadel (for comparison)[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/running-off-citadel.html#citadel-for-comparison)

| Concern | How it works |
| --- | --- |
| Traffic | One container per app, behind Citadel's front-end proxy (HA-Proxy). |
| Trusted proxies | `HELMET_PRESET=citadel`: trust only the proxy in front, never `*` (W17). |
| Logs | `php://stderr`, captured by the platform. File logging is the one case where a path is tolerated here: legacy apps wrote `storage/logs/laravel.log` **(check)**. The portable baseline keeps `storage/logs` empty (W14). |
| Writable paths | `storage/`, `bootstrap/cache/`. |
| User | Set by the Citadel image **(check)**. |
| Health | `/up`. |
| Queue | No queue workers on Citadel. The scheduled-worker mode `WELD_QUEUE_MODE=scheduled` is planned, not built (W19, **check**). |
| After deploy | `php artisan weld:doctor` in the app container. |

### OpenShift[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/running-off-citadel.html#openshift)

| Concern | How it works |
| --- | --- |
| Traffic | The OpenShift router fronts the route and forwards to the pod. |
| Trusted proxies | `HELMET_PROXIES=<router address>`, and the same address in TRUSTED_PROXIES: trust the router only (W17). There is no `openshift` preset; setting one throws. |
| Logs | `php://stderr`; read them with `oc logs`. |
| Writable paths | `storage/`, `bootstrap/cache/`. |
| User | OpenShift assigns a random UID in group 0 with capabilities dropped (W13), so make both writable paths group-owned and group-writable before the pod starts: `chgrp -R 0 storage bootstrap/cache && chmod -R g=u storage bootstrap/cache`. |
| Health | Liveness probe: HTTP GET `/up`. It answers for any `Host` over plain HTTP, before trusted hosts, sessions and auth (W11). |
| After deploy | `oc exec deploy/<app> -- php artisan weld:doctor`. |

### Coolify[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/running-off-citadel.html#coolify)

| Concern | How it works |
| --- | --- |
| Traffic | Coolify's Traefik instance fronts the app and routes by domain. |
| Trusted proxies | `HELMET_PROXIES=<Traefik container address>`, and the same address in TRUSTED_PROXIES (W17). There is no `coolify` preset; setting one throws. |
| Logs | `php://stderr`; Coolify shows the container logs. |
| Writable paths | `storage/`, `bootstrap/cache/`, on a persistent volume so they survive redeploys. |
| User | Whatever the image declares; keep it non-root (W13). |
| Health | A Dockerfile `HEALTHCHECK` that calls `/up` takes precedence over the dashboard check; either way the image needs `curl` or `wget` (W12). Traefik stops routing to an unhealthy container. |
| After deploy | Exec into the app container and run `php artisan weld:doctor`. |

### Plain Docker compose[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/running-off-citadel.html#plain-docker-compose)

| Concern | How it works |
| --- | --- |
| Traffic | Direct to the container, or your own reverse proxy in front. With no proxy, trust no forwarded headers: `HELMET_PRESET=docker` **(check)** (W17). |
| Logs | `php://stderr`; follow them with `docker compose logs -f app`. |
| Writable paths | Mount `storage/` and `bootstrap/cache/` as volumes so data survives the container. |
| User | Non-root `USER` in the image (W13). |
| Health | `HEALTHCHECK` on `/up` in the image (W12). |
| After deploy | `docker compose exec app php artisan weld:doctor`. |

The `compose.yaml` in this repository is the local development stack, not a production image. A production image for raw Docker is **(check)** until one ships.

Four tables, one bead: if the joint passes `weld:doctor` on all of them, the seam holds.

---

Source: https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/troubleshooting.html

## Troubleshooting[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/troubleshooting.html#troubleshooting)

This page covers the failures that trip people up in WELD, with the cause of each, the fix, and a command to check that it holds again.

### Symptoms[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/troubleshooting.html#symptoms)

Each entry follows the same shape: what you see, why it happens, how to fix it, and the command that proves it holds.

#### `composer ci` fails because the docs site is stale[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/troubleshooting.html#composer-ci-fails-because-the-docs-site-is-stale)

**Cause.** The docs at `site/docs/` are built from `docs/` by the shared docs builder, and `composer ci` runs `composer docs:check`, which fails when the committed docs site is stale or the docs carry findings. Change a page in `docs/` or `CHANGELOG.md` without rebuilding, and the check fails.

**Fix.** Rebuild the site from the source and commit the output. Do not edit `site/` by hand; the builder writes it, so the page you read is the page that ships.

```
composer docs
```

`composer docs` writes `site/docs/` from `docs/` and generates `docs/changelog.md` from `CHANGELOG.md`.

**Check.** Run the same check that `composer ci` runs; it writes nothing:

```
composer docs:check
```

#### The agent-ready files are stale[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/troubleshooting.html#the-agent-ready-files-are-stale)

**Cause.** The agent-ready site (prompt blocks, Markdown twins, llms.txt) comes from Squire's kit and is generated into `site/`. `composer ci` runs `composer site:agent-ready-check`, which fails when the agent-ready files are stale, a page lacks its Markdown link, a prompt drifts from the docs, or the kit was edited here.

**Fix.** Regenerate the files and commit the result:

```
composer site:agent-ready
```

That rewrites the Markdown twins, llms.txt, llms-full.txt, robots.txt and sitemap.xml in `site/`.

**Check.**

```
composer site:agent-ready-check
```

#### regen-check reports new drift[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/troubleshooting.html#regen-check-reports-new-drift)

**Cause.** The regen gate compares a freshly generated Sourdough Inertia app with WELD file by file, from Sourdough's `.sourdough/manifest.json` (each path with its SHA-256). It skips the product files listed in `.sourdough/product-files.json` and any `vendor` or `node_modules` path, and reports each remaining path as IDENTICAL, DIFFERS, MISSING_IN_WELD or RELOCATED (a Squire kit file WELD keeps byte-identical under `deploy/`). The gate is a ratchet: `.sourdough/regen-baseline.json` records the drift already known and accepted, and the check fails only on new drift, so a change in what Sourdough generates surfaces here.

**Fix.** Fix the drift here or upstream in Sourdough. If the drift is accepted as intended, record the current drift as accepted and commit `.sourdough/regen-baseline.json`:

```
php bin/regen-check.php --generated <dir> --write-baseline
```

Note

The regen gate is not part of `composer ci`. CI runs it as a separate, warning-only job, and the GitHub pipeline keeps it warning-only with `continue-on-error` until the baseline is filled in.

**Check.** Re-run the check against your own generation; it passes once every path is IDENTICAL or already recorded in the baseline:

```
php bin/regen-check.php --generated <dir>
```

Through Composer the same check is `composer regen-check -- --generated <dir>`.

### Related[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/troubleshooting.html#related)

- [Is WELD still Sourdough's shape?](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/regen-check.html)
- [Check your setup](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/check-your-setup.html)

---

Source: https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html

## Upgrading[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#upgrading)

This page shows how to keep a WELD app current: how to take stack changes, how to read the CHANGELOG, what a release does, and whether any released version breaks your app.

### Take stack changes[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#take-stack-changes)

WELD owns its app code. The wiring files are marked and refreshed by `sourdough feed`, not hand-edited, so the app does not fork from the stack. Sourdough is not a dependency yet, so there is no feed to run today; the target is for WELD's CI to run `sourdough feed` against each stack release and fail on drift.

When HELMET, SESAME, CREED or PROCTOR releases, raise the constraint here, run all the checks, and commit the lock file:

```sh
composer require waynestate/<part>:^0.x
bin/weld.sh test
```

```powershell
composer require waynestate/<part>:^0.x
.\bin\weld.ps1 test
```

`<part>` is the lowercase package name: `helmet`, `sesame`, `creed` or `proctor`.

When Laravel, Inertia or Vue release, Booster's hops are the way to move; WELD is a good first test for them.

After route changes, regenerate Ziggy and commit the result:

```sh
composer ziggy
git diff --exit-code resources/js/ziggy.*
```

When Sourdough changes what it generates, the regen gate flags the new drift in CI. Fix it here or upstream in Sourdough; if the drift is accepted as intended, record it with `--write-baseline` and commit `.sourdough/regen-baseline.json`.

### Read the CHANGELOG[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#read-the-changelog)

The CHANGELOG lists notable changes to WELD, newest first. Pending work sits under `## Unreleased`; each released version sits under a `## X.Y.Z (YYYY-MM-DD)` heading. To find what moved, read the entries between your current version and the one you are moving to.

### What a release does[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#what-a-release-does)

WELD is tagged (0.1.0 through 0.1.2 so far). A release:

1. Moves the lines under `## Unreleased` in `CHANGELOG.md` to a new `## X.Y.Z (YYYY-MM-DD)` heading.
2. Needs all the checks green locally, then both pipelines green for that commit.
3. Runs a secrets scan of the history and checks that nothing internal (server names, people, IDs) is in the tree.
4. Tags `X.Y.Z` (no `v`) on nougat; the mirror carries the tag to GitHub.
5. Needs a maintainer's approval. Never move or delete a published tag.

### Breaking changes[#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#breaking-changes)

No released version (0.1.0, 0.1.1, 0.1.2) carries a breaking change yet, so upgrading is just taking in the new release:

```sh
composer require waynestate/<part>:^0.x
```

Then run all the checks and commit the lock file.
